translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Twenty

sentences.zh: 徐陵子儉 弟孝克

translations.literal: Xu Ling, styled Zijian; his younger brother Xiaoke
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling, styled Zijian; his younger brother Xiaoke

sentences.zh: 徐陵字孝穆，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ling, styled Xiaomu, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling, styled Xiaomu, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖超之，齊鬱林太守，梁員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chaozhi was Administrator of Yulin under Qi and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Outside the Body under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chaozhi had been administrator of Yulin under Qi and an outside-body regular attendant of the scattered cavalry under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父摛，梁戎昭將軍、太子左衛率，贈侍中、太子詹事，諡貞子。

translations.literal: His father Chi was Rongzhao General and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard under Liang; posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi had been a Rongzhao general and left commandant of the heir apparent's guard under Liang; posthumously he was made palace attendant and grand mentor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 母臧氏，嘗夢五色雲化而為鳳，集左肩上，已而誕陵焉。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Zang, once dreamed that five-colored clouds transformed into a phoenix and alighted on her left shoulder; afterward she bore Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zang, once dreamed that five-colored clouds turned into a phoenix and settled on her left shoulder; soon after, she bore Ling.

sentences.zh: 時寶誌上人者，世稱其有道，陵年數歲，家人攜以候之，寶誌手摩其頂，曰「天上石麒麟也。

translations.literal: At the time the monk Baozhi was called a man of the Way in the world; when Ling was several years old his family brought him to call on him, and Baozhi stroked his crown and said, "A stone qilin from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Baozhi was held in his day to possess the Way. When Ling was only a few years old his family brought him to call. Baozhi laid a hand on his crown and said, "A stone qilin from heaven.

sentences.zh: 」光宅惠雲法師每嗟陵早成就，謂之顏回。

translations.literal: " The Guangzha monk Huiyun often sighed over Ling's early attainment and called him a Yan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: " The Guangzha monk Huiyun often marveled at how soon Ling came into his own and called him a Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 八歲，能屬文。

translations.literal: At eight he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could compose literary pieces.

sentences.zh: 十二，通莊老義。

translations.literal: At twelve he mastered the meanings of Zhuangzi and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he had mastered Zhuangzi and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 既長，博涉史籍，縱橫有口辯。

translations.literal: When grown he ranged widely through historical records and was skilled in disputation.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he ranged widely through histories and was quick and forceful in debate.

sentences.zh: 梁普通二年，晉安王為平西將軍、寧蠻校尉，〔一〕父摛為王諮議，王又引陵參寧蠻府軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong under Liang, the Prince of Jin'an was made General Who Pacifies the West and Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians; Editorial footnote marker 1. his father Chi was the prince's advising officer, and the prince also brought Ling in as military aide on the Pacify-the-Miao staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year 2 (521), the Prince of Jin'an was made general who pacifies the west and colonel pacifying the barbarians. [1] His father Chi served as the prince's advising officer, and the prince also brought Ling onto the Pacify-the-Miao staff as military aide.

sentences.zh: 〔中〕大通

translations.literal: Collation variant: [middle]; Datong.
translations.idiomatic: (Middle)/Datong

translations.literal: (two).
translations.idiomatic: (two)/

sentences.zh: 〔三〕年，王立為皇太子，〔二〕東宮置學士，陵充其選。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [three] year; adopted reading: In the second year the Prince was established as heir apparent, Editorial footnote marker 2. the eastern palace set up academicians, and Ling was chosen for the post.
translations.idiomatic: (three)/In the second year the Prince was established as heir apparent; [2] the eastern palace set up academicians, and Ling was chosen among them.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書度支郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Clerk for Revenue in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by degrees to clerk for revenue in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出為上虞令，御史中丞劉孝儀與陵先有隙，風聞劾陵在縣贓汙，因坐免。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Shangyu; the censor-in-chief Liu Xiaoyi and Ling had long borne a grudge, and on rumor he impeached Ling for corruption in the county, whereupon Ling was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Shangyu. Censor-in-chief Liu Xiaoyi, who had long borne a grudge against him, impeached him on rumor for corruption in the county, and Ling was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為南平王府行參軍，遷通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled as staff officer in the Prince of Nanping's establishment and was promoted to Direct and Upright Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as a staff officer to the Prince of Nanping and promoted to direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮撰長春殿義記，使陵為序。

translations.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace he compiled the Record of the Meaning of the Ever-Spring Hall and had Ling write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: While Liang's Emperor Jianwen was still in the eastern palace he compiled the Record of the Meaning of the Ever-Spring Hall and had Ling write the preface.

sentences.zh: 又令於少傅府述所製莊子義。

translations.literal: He also ordered him at the Junior Tutor's office to expound the Zhuangzi commentary he had composed.
translations.idiomatic: He also had him expound his Zhuangzi commentary at the junior tutor's office.

sentences.zh: 尋遷鎮西湘東王中記室參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Central Secretary to the Prince of Xiangdong, Pacifier of the West.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made central secretary to the Prince of Xiangdong, pacifier of the west.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，兼通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was made Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing year 2 (548) he was made concurrent regular attendant of the direct and upright scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 使魏，魏人授館宴賓。

translations.literal: He was sent on embassy to Wei; the people of Wei lodged him and feasted him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent on embassy to Wei. The Wei lodged him and feasted him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 是日甚熱，其主客魏收嘲陵曰：「今日之熱，當由徐常侍來。

translations.literal: That day was very hot; the chief host Wei Shou mocked Ling, saying, "Today's heat must be because Attendant Xu has come.
translations.idiomatic: That day was fiercely hot. The chief host, Wei Shou, mocked him: "Today's heat must be because Attendant Xu has come.

sentences.zh: 」陵即答曰：「昔王肅至此，為魏始制禮儀；

translations.literal: " Ling answered at once, "In former days when Wang Su came here, he first gave Wei its rites and ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: " Ling answered at once, "When Wang Su came here of old, he first gave Wei its rites and ceremonies;

sentences.zh: 今我來聘，使卿復知寒暑。

translations.literal: now that I have come on embassy, I have let you know again cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: now that I have come on embassy, I have taught you again the difference between cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 」收大慚。

translations.literal: " Wei Shou was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Shou was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇京師，陵父摛先在圍城之內，陵不奉家信，便蔬食布衣，若居憂恤。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raided the capital, Ling's father Chi was first inside the besieged city; Ling received no letters from home and at once took to vegetables and plain cloth, as if in mourning and distress.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided the capital, Ling's father Chi was trapped inside the siege. Ling received no word from home and at once ate plain food and wore coarse cloth, as though in mourning.

sentences.zh: 會齊受魏禪，梁元帝承制於江陵，復通使於齊。

translations.literal: It happened that Qi received the Mandate from Wei; Emperor Yuan of Liang held provisional rule at Jiangling and again exchanged envoys with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi then received the mandate from Wei. Emperor Yuan of Liang held provisional rule at Jiangling and again exchanged envoys with Qi.

sentences.zh: 陵累求復命，終拘留不遣，陵乃致書於僕射楊遵彥曰：

translations.literal: Ling repeatedly asked to be sent home with his mission, but in the end was detained and not released; Ling then addressed a letter to the Left Vice Director Yang Zunyian, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ling repeatedly asked leave to return with his mission, but was detained and not released. He then wrote to Vice Director Yang Zunyian:

sentences.zh: 夫一言所感，凝暉照於魯陽，一志冥通，飛泉涌於疏勒，況復元首康哉，股肱良哉，鄰國相聞，風教相期者也？

translations.literal: A single word that moves can make condensed radiance shine on Luoyang; a single will in dark communion can make flying springs gush at Shule—how much more when the head is hale and the limbs good, when neighboring states hear of one another and set their hearts on shared instruction?
translations.idiomatic: A single word that stirs the heart can hold the sun fast over Luoyang; a single will in hidden accord can make springs burst forth at Shule—how much more when ruler and ministers are sound, when neighboring states hear one another and look to shared teaching?

sentences.zh: 天道窮剝，鍾亂本朝，情計馳惶，公私哽懼，而骸骨之請徒淹歲寒，顛沛之祈空盈卷軸，是所不圖也，非所仰望也。

translations.literal: Heaven's way is exhausted and stripped; chaos has struck our court. Plans race in panic, public and private alike choke with fear—yet the plea to return home merely drags through a year of cold, and prayers in distress fill scroll after scroll in vain. This is not what I foresaw, nor what I hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is stripped bare; chaos has struck our court. In public and private alike fear chokes the throat—yet my plea to go home only drags through another winter, and scrolls of desperate prayer pile up unanswered. I never foresaw this. I never hoped for it.

sentences.zh: 執事不聞之乎！

translations.literal: Have you, sir, not heard?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not heard, sir?

sentences.zh: 昔分鼇命鳸之世，觀河拜洛之年，則有日

translations.literal: In former ages when the tortoise was divided and the pheasant ordained, in years when the river was viewed and Luo received, then there were days of
translations.idiomatic: In ages when Yu apportioned the turtle and commanded the pheasant, when Tang viewed the river and bowed to the Luo, there came sun-

translations.literal: Collation variant: (bird).
translations.idiomatic: (bird)/(crow)

sentences.zh: 〔烏〕流災，〔三〕風禽騁暴，天傾西北，地缺東南，盛旱坼三川，長波含五嶽。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [crow]; calamities flowed, Editorial footnote marker 3. wind-birds rampaged wildly, heaven tilted northwest, earth gaped southeast, fierce drought split the three rivers, long waves swallowed the five peaks.
translations.idiomatic: -calamities in flood, [3] wind-birds rampaged wild, heaven leaned northwest, earth gaped in the southeast, fierce drought split the three rivers, and long waves swallowed the five peaks.

sentences.zh: 我大梁應金圖而有亢，纂玉鏡而猶屯。

translations.literal: Our great Liang answered the golden chart yet met with obstruction; it inherited the jade mirror yet still was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Our great Liang answered the golden chart yet met obstruction; it took up the jade mirror yet still was stalled.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 聖人不能為時，斯固窮通之恆理也。

translations.literal: The sage cannot make the times—this is the constant principle of adversity and success.
translations.idiomatic: A sage cannot make the times—that is the constant law of rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 至如荊州刺史湘東王，機神之本，無寄名言，陶鑄之餘，猶為堯、舜，雖復六代之舞，陳於總章，九州之歌，登於司樂，虞夔拊石，晉曠調鍾，未足頌此英聲，無以宣其盛德者也。

translations.literal: As for the Governor of Jingzhou, the Prince of Xiangdong—the root of his subtle spirit cannot be lodged in words; what his molding leaves behind is still Yao and Shun. Though the dances of the six dynasties were displayed in the Hall of Total Brilliance and the songs of the nine regions were raised in the Office of Music, though Kui of Yu struck the stone and Kuang of Jin tuned the bell, they would not suffice to praise this heroic renown or declare such overflowing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Prince of Xiangdong, governor of Jingzhou—the root of his subtle spirit cannot be put into words; what his molding leaves is still Yao and Shun. Though the dances of six dynasties were set out in the Hall of Total Brilliance and the songs of nine regions were raised in the Office of Music, though Kui of Yu struck stone and Kuang of Jin tuned bells, none of it would suffice to praise his heroic renown or declare such overflowing virtue.

sentences.zh: 若使郊禋楚翼，寧非祀夏之君，戡定艱難，便是匡周之霸，豈徒豳王徙雍，期月為都，姚帝遷河，周年成邑。

translations.literal: If suburban sacrifice were offered on Chu wings, would he not be the lord who sacrificed to Xia? If he quelled hardship and danger, he would be the hegemon who restored Zhou—how much less only a King of Bin moving to Yong and making a capital in a month, or Emperor Yao of Yao moving to the river and completing a city in a year.
translations.idiomatic: If he offered suburban sacrifice on Chu wings, would he not be the lord who restored Xia? If he quelled hardship and danger, he would be the hegemon who righted Zhou—not merely a King of Bin moving to Yong and making a capital in a month, or Emperor Yao of Yao moving to the river and finishing a city in a year.

sentences.zh: 方今越常藐藐，〔四〕馴雉北飛，肅眘茫茫，風牛南偃，吾君之子，含識知歸，而答旨云何所投身，斯其未喻一也。

translations.literal: Today Yuechang is remote, Editorial footnote marker 4. tame pheasants fly north; Sushen stretches endless, wind and cattle lie south. Sons of our lord who have understanding know where to return—yet your reply asks where we should cast ourselves. This is what I do not understand, the first point.
translations.idiomatic: Today Yuechang lies far away, [4] tame pheasants fly north; Sushen stretches without end, wind and cattle lie down in the south. Sons of our lord who have sense know where to return—yet your reply asks where we should cast ourselves. That is my first point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 又晉熙等郡，皆入貴朝，去我尋陽，經塗何幾。

translations.literal: Moreover, commanderies such as Jingxi have all entered your honored court; from our Xunyang, how many stages lie on the road?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, commanderies such as Jingxi have all entered your honored court. From our Xunyang, how many stages lie on the road?

sentences.zh: 至於鐺鐺曉漏，的的宵烽，隔漵浦而相聞，臨高臺而可望。

translations.literal: As for the clanging dawn watch and the bright night beacons, we hear one another across the Mian ford and can look across from the high tower.
translations.idiomatic: The clanging dawn watch and the bright night beacons—we hear one another across the Mian ford and can look across from the high tower.

sentences.zh: 泉流寶碗，〔五〕遙憶湓城，峰號香鑪，依然廬嶽。

translations.literal: Springs flow in precious bowls, Editorial footnote marker 5. and from afar we recall Pen city; a peak called Incense Burner—still the Lu Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Springs flow in precious bowls, [5] and from afar we recall Pen city; a peak called Incense Burner—still the Lu Mountains.

sentences.zh: 日者鄱陽嗣王治兵匯派，屯戍淪波，朝夕牋書，春秋方物，吾無從以躡屩，彼何路而齊鑣。

translations.literal: Recently the heir prince of Poyang drilled troops where rivers meet and garrisoned the drowned waves; morning and evening he sent memorials, spring and autumn he sent tribute. I have no way to follow in straw sandals—by what road do they keep equal pace?
translations.idiomatic: Only lately the heir prince of Poyang drilled troops where rivers meet and garrisoned the drowned waves; morning and evening he sent memorials, in spring and autumn he sent tribute. I have no way to follow on foot in straw sandals—by what road do they keep equal pace?

sentences.zh: 豈其然乎？

translations.literal: Could that be so?
translations.idiomatic: Could that be so?

sentences.zh: 斯不然矣。

translations.literal: It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: It is not so.

sentences.zh: 又近者邵陵王通和此國，郢中上客，雲聚魏都，鄴下名卿，風馳江浦，豈盧龍之徑於彼新開，銅駝之街於我長閉？

translations.literal: Moreover, not long ago the Prince of Shaoling made peace with this state; honored guests from Ying gathered like clouds in the Wei capital, famous ministers from Ye raced like wind to the Jiang shore. Has the road through Lulong only now been opened for them, while the Street of Bronze Camels stays long shut for us?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, not long ago the Prince of Shaoling made peace with your state: honored guests from Ying gathered like clouds in the Wei capital, famous ministers from Ye raced like wind to the Jiang shore. Has the road through Lulong only now been opened for them, while the Street of Bronze Camels stays long shut for us?

sentences.zh: 何彼途甚易，非勞於五丁，我路為難，如登於九折？

translations.literal: Why is their road so easy, not laboring the five strong men, while our road is hard, like climbing nine bends?
translations.idiomatic: Why is their road so easy that it needs no labor of the five strong men, while our road is hard as climbing nine bends?

sentences.zh: 地不私載，何其爽歟？

translations.literal: Earth does not favor one carriage—how clear is that!
translations.idiomatic: Earth bears all alike—how plainly fair is that!

sentences.zh: 而答旨云還路無從，斯所未喻二也。

translations.literal: Yet your reply says there is no way home. This is what I do not understand, the second point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your reply says there is no way home. That is my second point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 晉熙、廬江，義陽、安陸，皆云款附，非復危邦，計彼中途，便當靜晏。

translations.literal: Jingxi, Lujiang, Yiyang, and Anlu all say they have submitted in good faith and are no longer perilous states; counting the middle of the road, they should already be calm and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi, Lujiang, Yiyang, and Anlu all say they have submitted in good faith and are no longer perilous states; count the middle of the road, and they should already be calm and settled.

sentences.zh: 自斯以北，桴鼓不鳴，自此以南，封疆未壹。

translations.literal: From there northward, drums and rattles do not sound; from here southward, the borders are not yet unified.
translations.idiomatic: From there northward, drums and rattles do not sound; from here southward, the borders are not yet unified.

sentences.zh: 如其境外，脫殞輕軀，幸非邊吏之羞，何在匹夫之命。

translations.literal: If beyond those borders one should chance to lose one's light body, it would be no shame to a frontier officer—why should a common man's life matter?
translations.idiomatic: If beyond those borders one should chance to lose one's slight body, it would be no frontier officer's shame—why should a common man's life matter?

sentences.zh: 又此賓遊，〔六〕通無貨殖，忝非韓起聘鄭，私買玉環，吳札過徐，躬要寶劍。

translations.literal: Moreover, on this guest journey Editorial footnote marker 6. there is no trade in goods; I am no Han Qi on embassy to Zheng buying a jade ring in private, no Wu Zha passing through Xu demanding a treasured sword in person.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on this guest journey [6] there is no trade in goods. I am no Han Qi on embassy to Zheng buying a jade ring in private, no Wu Zha passing Xu demanding a treasured sword in person.

sentences.zh: 由來宴錫，凡厥囊裝，行役淹留，皆已虛罄，散有限之微財，供無期之久客，斯可知矣。

translations.literal: From the first, feasts and gifts—every bag and bundle—through the long delay of travel have all been emptied; scattering limited small funds to supply an endless long stay abroad—this may be known.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, every feast and gift, every bag and bundle, has been emptied by long delay on the road. I scatter limited small funds to supply an endless stay abroad—that, you may know.

sentences.zh: 且據圖刎首，愚者不為，運斧全身，庸流所鑒。

translations.literal: Moreover, to seize a map and cut one's throat—fools do not do it; to wield an axe and preserve the whole body—even the vulgar take it as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: To seize a map and cut one's throat—fools do not do it. To wield an axe and preserve the whole body—even the vulgar take it as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 生輕一髮，自重千鈞，不以賈盜明矣。

translations.literal: Life is lighter than a single hair, heavier than a thousand jun—this is clear without needing a merchant-thief.
translations.idiomatic: Life is lighter than a single hair and heavier than a thousand jun—that needs no merchant-thief to make it clear.

sentences.zh: 骨肉不任充鼎俎，皮毛不足入貨財，盜有道焉，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: Flesh and bone cannot fill cauldrons and platters; skin and fur are not worth entering as goods for sale. There is a Way even for thieves—I have no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh and bone cannot fill cauldrons and platters; skin and fur are not worth selling as goods. Even thieves have a Way—I have no worry.

sentences.zh: 又公家遣使，脫有資須，本朝非隆平之時，遊客豈皇華之勢。

translations.literal: Moreover, if the government sends envoys and there should be needs, our court is not in a time of great peace, and a traveler cannot bear the majesty of the splendid envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if the government sends envoys and there should be needs, our court is not in a time of great peace, and a traveler cannot bear the majesty of the splendid envoy.

sentences.zh: 輕裝獨宿，非勞聚柝之儀，微騎閒行，寧望輶軒之禮。

translations.literal: Light baggage and lodging alone are not the labor of the rite of gathered watch-clappers; a few horsemen traveling at ease cannot look for the ceremony of the envoy's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Light baggage and lodging alone are not the labor of the rite of gathered watch-clappers; a few horsemen traveling at ease cannot expect the ceremony of the envoy's carriage.

sentences.zh: 歸人將從，私具驢騾，緣道亭郵，唯希蔬粟。

translations.literal: Those returning will follow with private donkeys and mules; along the road at post stations I only hope for vegetables and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Those returning will follow with private donkeys and mules; along the road at post stations I ask only for vegetables and grain.

sentences.zh: 若曰留之無煩於執事，遣之有費於官司，或以顛沛為言，或云資裝可懼，固非通論，皆是外篇。

translations.literal: If one says that to detain us gives no trouble to the officer in charge, while to send us off costs the government offices, or takes distress as an argument, or says traveling funds are to be feared—that is no proper discussion at all; all are side issues.
translations.idiomatic: If one says that to detain us gives no trouble to the officer in charge, while to send us off costs the government offices, or takes distress as an argument, or says traveling funds are to be feared—that is no proper discussion at all. All are side issues.

sentences.zh: 斯所未喻三也。

translations.literal: This is what I do not understand, the third point.
translations.idiomatic: That is my third point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 又若以吾徒應還侯景，侯景凶逆，殲我國家，天下含靈，人懷憤厲，既不獲投身社稷，衛難乘輿，四冢磔蚩尤，〔七〕千刀剸王莽，安所謂俛首頓膝，歸奉寇讎，珮弭腰鞬，為其皂隸？

translations.literal: Moreover, if you say our party ought to return to Hou Jing—Hou Jing is fierce and rebellious and has destroyed our state; all under heaven who have breath harbor indignation. Since we could not throw ourselves into the altars of soil and grain or guard the imperial carriage in peril, we should have the four quarters dismember Chiyou Editorial footnote marker 7. or a thousand blades carve Wang Mang—how then speak of bowing the head and bending the knee to return and serve the bandit foe, wearing bow and sword at the waist to be his menial?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if you say we ought to return to Hou Jing—Hou Jing is fierce and rebellious and has destroyed our state. All who draw breath under heaven harbor rage. We could not throw ourselves on the altars or guard the imperial carriage in peril; we should have had Chiyou torn on four mounds [7] and Wang Mang carved with a thousand blades—how then bow the head, bend the knee, return to serve the bandit foe, and wear bow and sword at the waist as his menial?

sentences.zh: 日者通和，方敦曩睦，凶人狙詐，遂駭狼心，頗疑宋萬之誅，彌懼荀罃之請，所以奔蹄勁角，專恣憑陵，凡我行人，偏膺讎憾。

translations.literal: Only lately peace was made and former friendship was thick; the fierce man lay in ambush with deceit and then startled the wolf's heart. I greatly feared the punishment of Song Wan and still more dreaded the plea of Xun Ying—therefore he ran with pounding hooves and sharp horns, indulging his will and lording it over others; every one of us travelers has borne his special hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Only lately peace was made and old friendship was thick; the fierce man crouched in deceit and then startled the wolf's heart. I feared a punishment like Song Wan's and dreaded still more a plea like Xun Ying's—so he ran with pounding hooves and sharp horns, indulging his will and lording it over all; every traveler in our party has borne his special hatred.

sentences.zh: 政復葅筋醢骨，抽舌探肝，於彼凶情，猶當未雪，海內之所知也，君侯之所具焉。

translations.literal: Even if we were pickled sinew and pounded bone, tongues drawn and livers probed, toward that fierce temper it would still not be enough to clear the score—this is what all within the seas know, and what you, my lord, are fully possessed of.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we were pickled sinew and pounded bone, tongues drawn and livers probed, toward that fierce temper it would still not clear the score—this all within the seas know, and what you, my lord, are fully possessed of.

sentences.zh: 又聞本朝公主，〔八〕都人士女，風行雨散，東播西流，京邑丘墟，姦蓬蕭瑟，偃師還望，咸為草萊，霸陵回首，俱沾霜露，此又君之所知也。

translations.literal: I also hear that the princesses of our court, Editorial footnote marker 8. ladies and women of the capital, were scattered by wind and rain, cast east and west; the capital is a ruin, wanton thickets rustle desolate; looking back on Yanshi, all has become wild grass; turning toward Baling, all are touched by frost and dew—this too is what you know.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that the princesses of our court, [8] ladies and women of the capital, were scattered by wind and rain, cast east and west; the capital is a ruin, wanton thickets rustle desolate; looking back on Yanshi, all has become wild grass; turning toward Baling, all are touched by frost and dew—this too you know.

sentences.zh: 彼以何義，爭免寇讎？

translations.literal: By what principle do they strive to escape the bandit foe?
translations.idiomatic: By what principle do they strive to escape the bandit foe?

sentences.zh: 我以何親，爭歸委質？

translations.literal: By what kinship do I strive to return and submit?
translations.idiomatic: By what kinship do I strive to return and submit?

sentences.zh: 昔鉅平貴將，懸重於陸公，叔向名流，深知於鬷篾。

translations.literal: In former days the honored general Juping hung heavy weight on Duke Lu; the famous man Shu Xiang was deeply known by Zong Mie.
translations.idiomatic: In former days the honored general Juping hung heavy weight on Duke Lu; the famous man Shu Xiang was deeply known by Zong Mie.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不敏，常慕前脩，不圖明庶有懷，翻其以此量物。

translations.literal: Though I am not clever, I have long admired those earlier exemplars; I did not expect that the enlightened multitude would harbor such feeling yet turn it to measure others in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not clever, I have long admired those earlier exemplars. I did not expect that the enlightened multitude would harbor such feeling yet turn it to measure others in this way.

sentences.zh: 昔魏氏將亡，群凶挺爭，諸賢戮力，想得其朋。

translations.literal: In former days when the house of Wei was about to perish, many fierce men rose in contention; the worthies joined their strength, thinking to gain their fellowship.
translations.idiomatic: In former days when the house of Wei was about to perish, many fierce men rose in contention; the worthies joined their strength, thinking to gain their fellowship.

sentences.zh: 為葛榮之黨邪？

translations.literal: Are we the party of Ge Rong?
translations.idiomatic: Are we the party of Ge Rong?

sentences.zh: 為邢杲之徒邪？

translations.literal: Are we the followers of Xing Gao?
translations.idiomatic: Are we the followers of Xing Gao?

sentences.zh: 如曰不然，斯所未喻四也。

translations.literal: If you say it is not so, this is what I do not understand, the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: If you say it is not so, that is my fourth point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 假使吾徒還為凶黨，侯景生於趙代，家自幽恆，居則台司，行為連率，山川形勢，軍國彝章，不勞請箸為籌，便當屈指能筭。

translations.literal: Suppose our party did return to the fierce faction: Hou Jing was born in Zhao and Dai; his family came from You and Heng; in residence he was terrace and minister, on campaign he was regional commander; the mountains and rivers, the forms of terrain, the military and civil statutes—without laboring to ask for chopsticks to reckon, he could count them on his fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose our party did return to the fierce faction: Hou Jing was born in Zhao and Dai; his family came from You and Heng; in residence he was terrace and minister, on campaign he was regional commander; mountains and rivers, terrain, military and civil statutes—without laboring to ask for chopsticks to reckon, he could count them on his fingers.

sentences.zh: 景以逋逃小醜，羊豕同群，身寓江皋，家留河朔，舂舂井井，〔九〕如鬼如神。

translations.literal: Jing was a fugitive petty villain of the same herd as sheep and swine; his person lodged on the river banks, his family remained in Heshuo; bustling and well-ordered, Editorial footnote marker 9. like a ghost, like a god.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was a fugitive petty villain of the same herd as sheep and swine; his person lodged on the river banks, his family remained in Heshuo; bustling and well-ordered, [9] like a ghost, like a god.

sentences.zh: 其不然乎？

translations.literal: Is that not so?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not so?

sentences.zh: 抑又君之所知也。

translations.literal: Or again, this is what you know.
translations.idiomatic: Or again, this you know.

sentences.zh: 且夫宮闈祕事，並若雲霄，英俊訏謨，寧非帷幄，或陽驚以定策，或焚稿而奏書，朝廷之士，猶難參預，羇旅之人，何階耳目。

translations.literal: Moreover, secret affairs of palace and inner quarters are all like clouds in the sky; heroic plans and counsel are surely not outside the command tent—some startled Yang to fix policy, some burned the draft to present the memorial. Men of the court still find it hard to take part; how should a man traveling abroad find a step to ear and eye?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, palace secrets are cloud-high; heroic counsel belongs in the command tent—some startled Yang to fix policy, some burned the draft before presenting the memorial. Courtiers still struggle to take part; how should a traveler abroad find a step to ear or eye?

sentences.zh: 至於禮樂沿革，刑政寬猛，則謳歌已遠，萬舞成風，不知手之舞之足之蹈之也。

translations.literal: As for the evolution of rites and music, the leniency or severity of punishments and government—then the songs of praise are already distant, the myriad dances have become custom; one no longer knows that the hands dance them and the feet tread them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the evolution of rites and music, the leniency or severity of punishments and government—the songs of praise are already distant, the myriad dances have become custom; one no longer knows that the hands dance them and the feet tread them.

sentences.zh: 安在搖其牙齒，為閒諜者哉？

translations.literal: Where is the need to wag one's teeth and be a spy in the gaps?
translations.idiomatic: Where is the need to wag one's teeth and be a spy in the gaps?

sentences.zh: 若謂復命西朝，終奔東虜，雖齊、梁有隔，尉候奚殊？

translations.literal: If you say that on returning to mission for the western court we would in the end flee to the eastern captive—though Qi and Liang are divided, how are the frontier guards different?
translations.idiomatic: If you say that on returning to mission for the western court we would in the end flee to the eastern captive—though Qi and Liang are divided, how are the frontier guards different?

sentences.zh: 豈以河曲之難浮，而曰江關之可濟？

translations.literal: How take the difficulty of floating at the river bend and yet say the river passes can be crossed?
translations.idiomatic: How take the difficulty of floating at the river bend and yet say the river passes can be crossed?

sentences.zh: 河橋馬度，寧非宋典之姦？

translations.literal: Horses crossing at the River Bridge—was that not the treachery of Song's canon?
translations.idiomatic: Horses crossing at the River Bridge—was that not the treachery of Song's canon?

sentences.zh: 關路雞鳴，皆曰田文之客。

translations.literal: Cocks crowing on the pass road—all are called the retainers of Tian Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Cocks crowing on the pass road—all are called the retainers of Tian Wen.

sentences.zh: 何其通蔽，乃爾相妨？

translations.literal: How penetrating and blind—thus to obstruct one another!
translations.idiomatic: How penetrating and blind—to obstruct one another so!

sentences.zh: 斯所未喻五也。

translations.literal: This is what I do not understand, the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fifth point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 又兵交使在，雖著前經，儻同徇僕之尤，追肆寒山之怒，則凡諸元帥，並釋縲囚，爰及偏裨，同無翦馘。

translations.literal: Moreover, though arms may clash while envoys remain—this is recorded in earlier classics—if it should be like the fault of the servant who died for his master, or the wrath vented on Cold Mountain pursued, then all the commanders would together release bound prisoners, down to junior officers, all alike without cutting down captives.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though arms may clash while envoys remain—this is recorded in earlier classics—if it should be like the fault of the servant who died for his master, or the wrath vented on Cold Mountain pursued, then all the commanders would together release bound prisoners, down to junior officers, all alike without cutting down captives.

sentences.zh: 乃至鍾儀見赦，朋笑遵途，襄老蒙歸，虞哥引路。

translations.literal: Down to Zhong Yi's being pardoned, Peng's laughter on the road of return; Xiang the elder receiving grace to go home, Yu Ge leading the way.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Zhong Yi's being pardoned, Peng's laughter on the road of return; Xiang the elder receiving grace to go home, Yu Ge leading the way.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕吾等張旜拭玉，脩好尋盟，涉泗之與浮河，郊勞至于贈賄，公恩既被，賓敬無違，今者何愆，翻蒙貶責？

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 10. We have spread banners and wiped jade, repaired good relations and sought alliance; crossing the Si and floating the river, suburban courtesy of labor extending to gifts on departure—your grace has already been shown, guest and host without breach. What fault is there now that we are turned instead to censure?
translations.idiomatic: [10] We have spread banners and wiped jade, repaired good relations and sought alliance; crossing the Si and floating the river, suburban courtesy of labor extending to gifts on departure—your grace has already been shown, guest and host without breach. What fault is there now that we are turned instead to censure?

sentences.zh: 若以此為言，斯所未喻六也。

translations.literal: If you take this as your argument, this is what I do not understand, the sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: If you take this as your argument, that is my sixth point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 若曰祅氛永久，喪亂悠然，哀我奔波，存其形魄，固已銘茲厚德，戴此洪恩，譬渤澥而俱深，方嵩華而猶重。

translations.literal: If you say evil vapors are long-lasting and ruin and chaos stretch on, pity our wandering toil and preserve our bodily souls—we have already engraved this deep kindness and bear this great grace, deep as the Bohai together, heavy still beside Song and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: If you say evil vapors are long-lasting and ruin and chaos stretch on, pity our wandering toil and preserve our bodily souls—we have already engraved this deep kindness and bear this great grace, deep as the Bohai together, heavy still beside Song and Hua.

sentences.zh: 但山梁飲啄，非有意於籠樊，江海飛浮，本無情於鍾鼓。

translations.literal: But the beam of the mountain drinks and pecks without intent for cage and fence; rivers and seas float and fly without feeling for bell and drum.
translations.idiomatic: But the beam of the mountain drinks and pecks without intent for cage and fence; rivers and seas float and fly without feeling for bell and drum.

sentences.zh: 況吾等營魂已謝，餘息空留，悲默為生，何能支久，是則雖蒙養護，更夭天年。

translations.literal: Moreover, our camp souls are already spent; remaining breath is left empty; grief and silence are our life—how can we endure long? Thus though we receive fostering care, we shorten our heaven-allotted years.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our camp souls are already spent; remaining breath is left empty; grief and silence are our life—how can we endure long? Thus though we receive fostering care, we shorten our heaven-allotted years.

sentences.zh: 若以此為言，斯所未喻七也。

translations.literal: If you take this as your argument, this is what I do not understand, the seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: If you take this as your argument, that is my seventh point of doubt.

sentences.zh: 若云逆豎殲夷，當聽反命，高軒繼路，飛蓋相隨，未解其言，何能善謔？

translations.literal: If you say the rebel villain must be destroyed before my return is heard, with high carriages one after another and flying canopies following in train—having not grasped such words, how could one jest well?
translations.idiomatic: If you say I may return only after the rebel is destroyed, with high coaches in endless file and flying canopies in train—I do not understand such words; how could one jest at all?

sentences.zh: 夫屯亨治亂，豈有意於前期。

translations.literal: Fortune and adversity, order and chaos—can they be foreseen beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and adversity, order and chaos—who can foresee them in advance?

sentences.zh: 謝常侍今年五十有一，吾今年四十有四，介已知命，賓又杖鄉，計彼侯生，肩隨而已。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Xie is fifty-one this year; I am forty-four. Both have reached the age of knowing fate; as guests we are already at the staff-and-village years. Counting that Hou Sheng, he is only a shoulder behind.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Xie is fifty-one this year; I am forty-four. We have both reached knowing fate; as envoys we are already at staff-and-village age. Counting that Hou fellow, he is barely a step behind us.

sentences.zh: 豈銀臺之要，彼未從師，金灶之方，吾知其決，〔一一〕政恐南陽菊水，竟不延齡，東海桑田，無由可望。

translations.literal: How could the essentials of the Silver Terrace be what he has not yet learned from a master, while the recipe of the Golden Stove is what I know the secret of? I truly fear that the chrysanthemum water of Nanyang will in the end not prolong life, and the mulberry fields of the Eastern Sea will have no day to be seen again.
translations.idiomatic: As if the Silver Terrace arts were what he had never studied, while I alone knew the Golden Stove secret! I fear Nanyang's chrysanthemum water will not prolong life after all, and the Eastern Sea's mulberry fields will never be seen again.

sentences.zh: 若以此為言，斯所未喻八也。

translations.literal: If you take this as your argument, this is what I fail to understand—eight.
translations.idiomatic: If that is your argument, this is what I fail to understand—the eighth point.

sentences.zh: 足下清襟勝託，書囿文林，凡自洪荒，終乎幽、厲，如吾今日，寧有其人，爰至春秋，微宜商略。

translations.literal: Your pure bosom rises above common trust; your garden of books and forest of letters—from primal chaos down to You and Li, is there today anyone like me? Down to the Spring and Autumn era, it would be fitting to discuss a little.
translations.idiomatic: Your refined mind towers above ordinary men; in books and letters—from primal chaos to the reigns of You and Li—is there anyone like me today? Even in Spring and Autumn times one might debate the point.

sentences.zh: 夫宗姬殄墜，霸道昏凶，或執政之多門，或陪臣之敘德，故臧孫有禮，翻囚與國之賓，周伯無愆，空怒天王之使，遷箕卿於兩館，縶驥子於三年。

translations.literal: When the Zhou royal house perished, hegemonic ways turned brutal; sometimes many factions held power, sometimes dependent ministers lacked virtue. Thus Zangsun, though possessed of rites, was turned into a prisoner and a guest of another state; the Earl of Zheng, though without fault, vainly roused the Son of Heaven's envoy to anger. The Viscount of Ji was moved to the Two Lodgings; the son of Ji was tethered for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou royal house fell, hegemonic power turned cruel; sometimes many hands held the government, sometimes vassal ministers lacked virtue. Zangsun had rites yet was made a prisoner and another state's guest; the Earl of Zheng was blameless yet needlessly provoked the Son of Heaven's envoy. The Viscount of Ji was lodged in the Two Pavilions; the son of Ji was bound for three years.

sentences.zh: 斯匪貪亂之風邪？

translations.literal: Is this not the wind of greedy disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not the breath of greedy disorder?

sentences.zh: 寧當今之高例也？

translations.literal: Can it be a lofty precedent for today?
translations.idiomatic: Can it be a lofty precedent for our age?

sentences.zh: 至於雙崤且帝，四海爭雄，或構趙而侵燕，或連韓而謀魏，身求盟於楚殿，躬奪璧於秦庭，輸寶鼎以託齊王，馳安車而誘梁客。

translations.literal: As for the time when the Twin Peaks were both emperors and the four seas contended for supremacy—sometimes they allied with Zhao to invade Yan, sometimes they linked with Han to plot against Wei; bodies sought alliance in the hall of Chu, persons snatched the jade disk in the court of Qin; they sent the precious tripod to entrust it to the King of Qi, galloped the comfort carriage to lure a guest of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Twin Peaks were both emperors and the four seas fought for mastery, some allied with Zhao to strike Yan, some joined Han against Wei; men sought treaties in Chu's halls and snatched jade in Qin's court; they sent the sacred tripod to Qi and drove the comfort carriage to lure Liang's guest.

sentences.zh: 其外膏脣販舌，〔一二〕分路揚鑣，無罪無辜，如兄如弟。

translations.literal: Beyond that, oily lips and trafficking tongues, each taking a different road and whip, innocent and guiltless as brothers one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that were slick tongues and peddled words, parting ways like brothers who were innocent alike.

sentences.zh: 逮乎中陽受命，天下同規，巡省諸華，無聞幽辱。

translations.literal: When Zhongyang received the Mandate, all under Heaven shared one measure; touring and inspecting the various Huaxia, none heard of hidden insult.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyang received the Mandate, the realm shared one standard; in touring the Huaxia, none heard of secret humiliation.

sentences.zh: 及三方之霸也，孫甘言以嫵媚，曹屈詐以羈縻，旍軫歲到於句吳，冠蓋年馳於庸蜀，則客嘲殊險，賓戲已深，共盡遊談，誰云猜忤。

translations.literal: When the three sides were hegemons, Sun used sweet words to flatter, Cao bent deceit to tether; banners and chariots came yearly to Gouwú, caps and coaches raced yearly to Yong-Shu. Then guests' mockery was especially perilous, hosts' sport already deep; together they exhausted wandering talk—who said there was suspicion and offense?
translations.idiomatic: Among the three hegemons, Sun flattered with honeyed words and Cao bound men with fraud; banners yearly reached Gouwú and coaches yearly sped to Yong-Shu. Guests' barbs grew sharp and hosts' games deep; they talked freely together—who spoke of suspicion?

sentences.zh: 若使搜求故實，脫有前蹤，恐是叔世之姦謀，而非為邦之勝略也。

translations.literal: If one were to search out old precedents and there chanced to be earlier traces, I fear they would be the treacherous schemes of a decadent age, not winning policies for governing a state.
translations.idiomatic: Search old precedents and any trace you find is likely a decadent age's treachery, not a state's winning strategy.

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，雲師火帝，澆淳乃異其風，龍躍麟驚，王霸雖殊其道，莫不崇君親以銘物，〔一三〕敦敬養以治民，預有邦司，曾無隆替。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard: Cloud Master and Fire Emperor—their flood and purity differed in custom; dragon leaping and unicorn startling—king and hegemon though different in the Way, none failed to honor ruler and kin to inscribe things and thicken respect and nurture to govern the people. There were always state officers; never was there rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard: Cloud Master and Fire Emperor differed in flood and purity; dragon and unicorn marked king and hegemon—yet all honored kin and ruler and thickened nurture to govern the people. States always had officers; ranks did not simply rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 吾奉違溫凊，仍屬亂離，寇虜猖狂，公私播越。

translations.literal: I have failed in warmth and coolness toward my parents and still belong to chaotic separation; bandits and foes run riot, public and private scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: I have failed my parents in warmth and coolness and still live in chaos; enemies run wild and public and private life are scattered.

sentences.zh: 蕭軒靡御，王舫誰持？

translations.literal: The Xiao carriage has none to drive it; who holds the royal boat?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage lacks a driver; who holds the royal boat?

sentences.zh: 瞻望鄉關，何心天地？

translations.literal: Gazing toward home and native district—what heart remains for Heaven and Earth?
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward home—what heart is left for Heaven and Earth?

sentences.zh: 自非生憑廩竹，源出空桑，行路含情，猶其相愍。

translations.literal: Unless one were born leaning on barn bamboo and sprung from the hollow mulberry, travelers on the road would still feel compassion and pity one another.
translations.idiomatic: Unless born of barn bamboo and hollow mulberry, wayfarers would still pity one another.

sentences.zh: 常謂擇官而仕，非曰孝家，擇事而趨，非云忠國。

translations.literal: I have always held that choosing an office to serve is not called filial to one's family; choosing an affair to hurry to is not said to be loyal to the state.
translations.idiomatic: I have always held that choosing an office is not filial piety, and choosing an errand is not loyalty to the state.

sentences.zh: 況乎欽承有道，驂駕前王，郎吏明經，鴟鳶知禮，巡省方化，〔一四〕咸問高年，東序西膠，〔一五〕皆尊耆耋。

translations.literal: How much more when reverently receiving the Way and driving in the train of former kings—court gentlemen who understand the classics, owls and kites who know rites; touring the regions to transform custom, all inquire after the aged; eastern school and western academy all honor the old.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one reverently receives the Way and rides with former kings—clerks who know the classics, owls and kites who know ritual; tours to transform custom ask after the aged; eastern and western academies honor the old.

sentences.zh: 吾以圭璋玉帛，通聘來朝，屬世道之屯期，鍾生民之否運，兼年累載，無申元直之祈，銜泣吞聲，長對公閭之怒，情禮之訴，將同逆鱗，忠孝之言，皆應齚舌，是所不圖也，非所仰望也。

translations.literal: I came with jade scepters and silks in friendly embassy; it happened to be a time of the world's hardship and struck the people's adverse fortune. For years piled on years I could not present the straight petition of the first month; swallowing tears and holding back sound, I long faced the public anger of the lanes. Pleas of feeling and rite would be like touching the inverse scale; words of loyalty and filial piety should all bite the tongue. This is what I did not plan for, not what I looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: I came with jade and silk on friendly embassy, only to meet the world's hardship and the people's ill fortune. Year on year I could not file the New Year's straight petition; choking back tears I long faced public wrath. Pleas of feeling and rite would touch the dragon's scale; words of loyalty and filial piety must be bitten off. That is what I never planned and never hoped for.

sentences.zh: 且天倫之愛，何得忘懷？

translations.literal: Moreover, love of Heaven's kin—how can it be forgotten from the heart?
translations.idiomatic: And love of Heaven's kin—how can the heart forget it?

sentences.zh: 妻子之情，誰能無累？

translations.literal: Feeling for wife and children—who can be without burden?
translations.idiomatic: Feeling for wife and children—who is without burden?

sentences.zh: 夫以清河公主之貴，餘姚書佐之家，莫限高卑，皆被驅略。

translations.literal: Even the Princess of Qinghe in her nobility and the book-assistant's household of Yuyao, without limit of high or low, were all driven off and seized.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Princess of Qinghe in her rank and the Yuyao clerk's household, high and low alike, were driven off and seized.

sentences.zh: 自東南醜虜，抄販饑民，臺署郎官，俱餒墻壁，況吾生離死別，多歷暄寒，孀室嬰兒，何可言念。

translations.literal: Since the ugly foe of the southeast trafficked in starving people, terrace-office gentlemen were all starved against the walls; how much more my partings in life and death, many seasons of cold and heat, a widow's chamber and infant child—what words can tell it?
translations.idiomatic: Since the southeast foe trafficked in the starving, terrace clerks starved against their walls; how much more my years of life-and-death parting, widow's room and infant—what words can tell it?

sentences.zh: 如得身還鄉土，躬自推求，猶冀提攜，俱免凶虐。

translations.literal: If I could return in person to my native soil and search with my own hands, I would still hope to lead them by the hand and together escape cruel abuse.
translations.idiomatic: If I could return home and search myself, I would still hope to lead them forth and together escape cruelty.

sentences.zh: 夫四聰不達，華陽君所謂亂臣，百姓無冤，孫叔敖稱為良相。

translations.literal: When the Four Hearings do not reach, Huayang Jun called such men rebellious ministers; when the common people have no grievance, Sun Shu'ao was termed a good minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Four Hearings fail, Huayang Jun called that a rebellious minister; when the people have no wrongs, Sun Shu'ao was called a good minister.

sentences.zh: 足下高才重譽，參贊經綸，非豹非貔，〔一六〕聞詩聞禮，而中朝大議，曾未矜論，清禁嘉謀，安能相及，諤諤非周舍，容容類胡廣，何其無諍臣哉？

translations.literal: You, sir, have lofty talent and heavy reputation and assist in state policy—not leopard, not bear, you have heard the Odes and heard the Rites; yet on great deliberations of the central court you have never once argued with dignity; on fine plans of the clear forbidden precinct how could you reach them? Blunt bluntness is not Zhou She; easy compliance resembles Hu Guang—how is there no remonstrating minister?
translations.idiomatic: You have lofty talent and weighty fame and assist state policy—you have heard Odes and Rites; yet on the court's great deliberations you have never argued; on the palace's fine plans how could you match them? Blunt speech is not Zhou She; easy compliance is Hu Guang—where are the remonstrating ministers?

sentences.zh: 歲月如流，平生何幾，晨看旅鴈，心赴江淮，昏望牽牛，情馳揚越，朝千悲而掩泣，夜萬緒而回腸，不自知其為生，不自知其為死也。

translations.literal: Years flow like water—how much of life remains? At dawn I watch the migrating geese and my heart races to the Jiang-Huai; at dusk I gaze at the Herd-Boy and feeling gallops to Yang-Yue. By day a thousand sorrows make me hide tears; by night ten thousand thoughts turn my entrails. I do not know myself as living; I do not know myself as dead.
translations.idiomatic: Years flow like water—how much life is left? At dawn I watch wild geese and my heart flies to Jiang-Huai; at dusk I gaze at the Herd-Boy and feeling races to Yang-Yue. By day a thousand griefs bring tears; by night ten thousand thoughts wring the gut. I scarcely know I live; I scarcely know I die.

sentences.zh: 足下素挺詞鋒，兼長理窟，匡丞相解頤之說，樂令君清耳之談，向所諮疑，誰能曉喻。

translations.literal: You, sir, have always wielded a sharp edge in words and are also long in the cave of principle—Chancellor Kuang's brow-relaxing discourse, Magistrate Yue's ear-clearing talk; of what I have consulted and doubted, who can make it clear?
translations.idiomatic: You have always had a sharp tongue and a deep grasp of principle—Chancellor Kuang's discourse that unknit the brow, Magistrate Yue's talk that cleared the ear; of my doubts, who can explain them?

sentences.zh: 若鄙言為謬，來旨必通，分請灰釘，甘從斧鑊，何但規規默默，齰舌低頭而已哉。

translations.literal: If my humble words are wrong, your coming letter will surely make it through; I ask only to be ashes and nails and gladly follow the axe and boiling cauldron—why merely stare in silence, bite the tongue, and bow the head?
translations.idiomatic: If my words err, your reply will surely clear them; I ask only to be ashes under the nail and gladly face axe and cauldron—why only stare, bite my tongue, and bow my head?

sentences.zh: 若一理存焉，猶希矜眷，何必期令我等必死齊都，足趙魏之黃塵，加幽并之片骨，遂使東平拱樹，長懷向漢之悲，西洛孤墳，恆表思鄉之夢。

translations.literal: If one principle remains, I still hope for your compassionate regard—why must you expect that we shall surely die in the capital of Qi, that our feet tread the yellow dust of Zhao and Wei, that our bones add a sliver to You and Bing? Thus the bowing trees of Dongping would long cherish grief toward Han; the lonely tomb of western Luoyang would ever show dreams of longing for home.
translations.idiomatic: If one point stands, I still hope for your mercy—why must you expect us to die in Qi's capital, feet in Zhao-Wei dust, bones adding to You-Bing? Then Dongping's bowing trees would long mourn toward Han; western Luoyang's lonely tomb would ever dream of home.

sentences.zh: 干祈以屢，哽慟增深。

translations.literal: Repeated pleas have made the choking grief deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated pleas have only deepened my choking grief.

sentences.zh: 遵彥竟不報書。

translations.literal: Zunyian in the end did not reply to the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyian never answered the letter.

sentences.zh: 及江陵陷，齊送貞陽侯蕭淵明為梁嗣，乃遣陵隨還。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Qi sent the Marquis of Zhenyuan Xiao Yuanming as Liang successor, and then dispatched Ling to return with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Qi sent the Marquis of Zhenyuan, Xiao Yuanming, as Liang successor and had Ling accompany him back.

sentences.zh: 太尉王僧辯初拒境不納，淵明往復致書，皆陵詞也。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian at first barred the border and would not receive them; Yuanming sent letters back and forth, all in Ling's wording.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian at first barred the border and refused entry; Yuanming exchanged letters, all drafted by Ling.

sentences.zh: 及淵明之入，僧辯得陵大喜，接待饋遺，其禮甚優。

translations.literal: When Yuanming entered, Sengbian was greatly delighted to obtain Ling, received and entertained him with gifts—his courtesy was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanming entered, Sengbian was overjoyed to have Ling, entertained him generously, and heaped gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 以陵為尚書吏部郎，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Ling was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was made director of the ministry of personnel in the masters of writing and handled edicts.

sentences.zh: 其年高祖率兵誅僧辯，仍進討韋載。

translations.literal: That year the Founder led troops to execute Sengbian and then advanced to attack Wei Zai.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Founder led troops to kill Sengbian and then marched against Wei Zai.

sentences.zh: 時任約、徐嗣徽乘虛襲石頭，陵感僧辯舊恩，乃往赴約。

translations.literal: At that time Ren Yue and Xu Sihui seized the moment to raid Stone City; Ling, moved by Sengbian's old kindness, then went to join Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ren Yue and Xu Sihui raided Stone City; Ling, remembering Sengbian's kindness, went to join Yue.

sentences.zh: 及約等平，高祖釋陵不問。

translations.literal: When Yue and the others were pacified, the Founder released Ling without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue and the rest were subdued, the Founder pardoned Ling without punishment.

sentences.zh: 尋以為貞威將軍、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Zhenwei General and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made zhenwei general and left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年，又使于齊，還除給事黃門侍郎、祕書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaotai he was again sent as envoy to Qi; on return he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presenting Matters and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 (555) he was again envoy to Qi; on return he was made attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate for presenting matters and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加散騎常侍，左丞如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry while the left vice director post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Ling was also made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry while keeping the left vice director post.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，除太府卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjia he was made Minister of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjia (560) he was made minister of the grand storehouse.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷五兵尚書，領大著作。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Minister of the Five Arms and concurrently Grand Director of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was moved to minister of the five arms and concurrently grand director of composition.

sentences.zh: 六年，除散騎常侍、御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and imperial censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時安成王頊為司空，〔一七〕以帝弟之尊，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, was Minister of Works; by the emperor's younger-brother rank his power bent the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, was minister of works; as the emperor's brother his power dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 直兵鮑僧叡假王威權，〔一八〕抑塞辭訟，大臣莫敢言者。

translations.literal: Straight guard Bao Sengrui borrowed the prince's authority, blocked and choked lawsuits, and great ministers dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Straight guard Bao Sengrui used the prince's power to choke off lawsuits, and great ministers dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 陵聞之，乃為奏彈，導從南臺官屬，引奏案而入。

translations.literal: When Ling heard of it, he drew up a memorial of impeachment, led attendants from the Southern Terrace, and entered presenting the case.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Ling drafted an impeachment memorial, led Southern Terrace attendants, and entered with the case.

sentences.zh: 世祖見陵服章嚴肅，若不可犯，為斂容正坐。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen saw Ling's memorial and bearing stern, as if he could not be violated, and composed his face to sit upright.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen saw Ling's stern memorial and bearing, as though he could not be touched, and straightened himself on the throne.

sentences.zh: 陵進讀奏版時，安成王殿上侍立，仰視世祖，流汗失色。

translations.literal: When Ling advanced to read the memorial board, the Prince of Ancheng stood attending in the hall, looking up at the emperor, sweating and losing color.
translations.idiomatic: As Ling read the memorial, the Prince of Ancheng stood in the hall, looked up at the emperor, and sweated pale.

sentences.zh: 陵遣殿中御史引王下殿，遂劾免侍中、中書監。

translations.literal: Ling sent a palace censor to lead the prince down from the hall and then impeached and removed him from attendant-in-ordinary and director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ling had a palace censor lead the prince down and impeached him from attendant-in-ordinary and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自此朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: From this the court was awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: From then the court was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，遷吏部尚書，領大著作。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was moved to Minister of Personnel and concurrently Grand Director of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 1 (566) he was moved to minister of personnel and concurrently grand director of composition.

sentences.zh: 陵以梁末以來，選授多失其所，於是提舉綱維，綜覈名實。

translations.literal: Ling, because from the end of Liang appointments and grants had mostly missed their proper targets, then raised the guiding cords and examined names against reality.
translations.idiomatic: Because since late Liang appointments had missed their mark, Ling raised standards and matched names to reality.

sentences.zh: 時有冒進求官，諠競不已者，陵乃為書宣示曰：「自古吏部尚書者，品藻人倫，簡其才能，尋其門冑，逐其大小，量其官爵。

translations.literal: At that time there were those who pushed forward rashly seeking office, clamoring without cease; Ling then issued a written proclamation, saying: "From antiquity those who were Ministers of Personnel assessed human relations, selected talent, traced lineage, followed great and small, and measured rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: When men clamored for office without end, Ling issued a proclamation: "From antiquity the minister of personnel assessed men, chose talent, traced lineage, weighed rank, and measured office.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承侯景之凶荒，王太尉接荊州之禍敗，爾時喪亂，無復典章，故使官方，窮此紛雜。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang inherited Hou Jing's cruel desolation; Grand Marshal Wang received Jingzhou's disaster and defeat—at that time mourning and chaos left no regulations, and so official ranks reached this tangle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang inherited Hou Jing's ruin; Grand Marshal Wang took Jingzhou's disaster—then mourning and chaos left no rules, and offices fell into this tangle.

sentences.zh: 永定之時，聖朝草創，干戈未息，亦無條序。

translations.literal: In the time of Yongding the holy court was newly founded, war had not ceased, and there was likewise no order.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding the new court was still at war and likewise had no order.

sentences.zh: 府庫空虛，賞賜懸乏，白銀難得，黃札易營，權以官階，代於錢絹，義存撫接，無計多少，致令員外、常侍，路上比肩，諮議、參軍，市中無數，豈是朝章，應其如此？

translations.literal: Treasury and storehouses were empty, rewards hung lacking; white silver was hard to obtain, yellow edicts easy to arrange—rank was used in place of cash and silk to comfort and connect, with no reckoning of amount, so that supernumerary attendants and regular attendants stood shoulder to shoulder on the road, consultants and staff officers were countless in the market. Was this what court regulations should be?
translations.idiomatic: Treasuries were empty and rewards scarce; white silver was hard to get and yellow edicts easy to trade—rank stood in for cash to comfort men, with no count of numbers, until supernumerary and regular attendants crowded the roads and consultants and staff officers filled the markets. Was that what court law should be?

sentences.zh: 今衣冠禮樂，日富年華，何可猶作舊意，非理望也。

translations.literal: Now caps, robes, rites, and music grow richer year by year—how can the old way still be followed? It is not reasonable expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Now rites and music grow richer each year—how can the old way still hold? That is not reasonable.

sentences.zh: 所見諸君，多踰本分，猶言大屈，未喻高懷。

translations.literal: Those I see, gentlemen, mostly exceed their proper measure and still say they suffer great constraint—they do not understand your lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: Most of you exceed your proper rank and still call it great constraint—you do not grasp your superiors' intent.

sentences.zh: 若問梁朝朱領軍异亦為卿相，此不踰其本分邪？

translations.literal: If one asks whether Zhu Yijun of Liang also became minister and chancellor—did he not exceed his measure?
translations.idiomatic: If you ask whether Liang's Zhu Yijun also became minister and chancellor—did he not exceed his measure?

sentences.zh: 此是天子所拔，非關選序。

translations.literal: That was the Son of Heaven's elevation; it had nothing to do with the selection sequence.
translations.idiomatic: That was the Son of Heaven's choice, not the selection process.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝云『世間人言有目色，我特不目色范悌』。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said, "Men of the world speak of having an eye for men; I alone have no eye for Fan Ti."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang said, "The world speaks of an eye for men; I alone have no eye for Fan Ti."

sentences.zh: 宋文帝亦云『人世豈無運命，每有好官缺，輒憶羊玄保。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song also said, "Does the human world lack fate? Whenever a fine office is vacant I always think of Yang Xuanbao."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song also said, "Does the world lack fate? Whenever a fine post opens I think of Yang Xuanbao."

sentences.zh: 』此則清階顯職，不由選也。

translations.literal: Thus clear ranks and conspicuous posts do not come through selection.
translations.idiomatic: Thus high offices do not come through selection.

sentences.zh: 秦有車府令趙高直至丞相，漢有高廟令田千秋亦為丞相，此復可為例邪？

translations.literal: In Qin the carriage-office director Zhao Gao rose straight to chancellor; in Han the high-temple director Tian Qianqiu also became chancellor—can these again serve as examples?
translations.idiomatic: In Qin the carriage-office director Zhao Gao rose to chancellor; in Han the high-temple director Tian Qianqiu did the same—are those examples?

sentences.zh: 既忝衡流，應須粉墨。

translations.literal: Having been entrusted with the current, one ought to apply ink.
translations.idiomatic: Having charge of the current, I must apply the ink.

sentences.zh: 所望諸賢，深明鄙意。

translations.literal: What I hope from you gentlemen is a deep understanding of my humble intent.
translations.idiomatic: I ask you gentlemen to understand my intent deeply.

sentences.zh: 」自是眾咸服焉，時論比之毛玠。

translations.literal: " From this all submitted in admiration; opinion of the time compared him to Mao Jie.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter all submitted; contemporaries compared him to Mao Jie.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，高宗入輔，謀黜異志者，引陵預其議。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Emperor Xuan entered to assist and, plotting to remove those of divergent intent, drew Ling into the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Emperor Xuan entered as regent and, planning to remove dissenters, drew Ling into counsel.

sentences.zh: 高宗纂曆，封建昌縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the calendar, he enfeoffed Ling as Marquis of Jianchang with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he enfeoffed Ling as Marquis of Jianchang, fief five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，除尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) he was made right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷尚書左僕射，〔一九〕陵抗表推周弘正、王勱等，高宗召陵入內殿，曰：「卿何為固辭此職而舉人乎？

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was moved to left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 」陵曰：「周弘正從陛下西還，舊藩長史，王勱太平相府長史，張種帝鄉賢戚，若選賢與舊，臣宜居後。

translations.literal: Ling submitted a memorial declining in favor of Zhou Hongzheng, Wang Li, and others. Emperor Xuan summoned Ling into the inner hall and said, "Why do you stubbornly decline this post and recommend others?"
translations.idiomatic: Ling memorialized to yield to Zhou Hongzheng, Wang Li, and others. Emperor Xuan summoned him and said, "Why stubbornly decline and recommend others?"

sentences.zh: 」固辭累日，高宗苦屬之，陵乃奉詔。

translations.literal: Ling said, "Zhou Hongzheng returned west with Your Majesty and was long the chief clerk of the old fief; Wang Li was chief clerk of the Taiping chancellor's office; Zhang Zhong is a worthy kinsman of the imperial district. If one chooses worthies of old service, I should stand behind."
translations.idiomatic: Ling said, "Zhou Hongzheng came west with Your Majesty and was long chief clerk of the old fief; Wang Li was chief clerk of the Taiping chancellor's office; Zhang Zhong is an imperial kinsman. Choose worthies of old service and I should stand behind."

sentences.zh: 及朝議北伐，高宗曰：「朕意已決，卿可舉元帥。

translations.literal: For days he stubbornly declined; Emperor Xuan urgently charged him, and Ling then accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He declined for days; Emperor Xuan pressed him, and Ling accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 」眾議咸以中權將軍淳于量位重，共署推之。

translations.literal: When the court deliberated a northern expedition, Emperor Xuan said, "My mind is already decided—you may nominate a commander-in-chief."
translations.idiomatic: When court debated a northern campaign, Emperor Xuan said, "My mind is set—nominate a commander."

sentences.zh: 陵獨曰：「不然。

translations.literal: In joint deliberation all thought Central Authority General Chunyu Liang, because of his weighty position, and together signed to push him.
translations.idiomatic: All thought Central Authority General Chunyu Liang weighty and jointly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹家在淮左，悉彼風俗，將略人才，當今亦無過者。

translations.literal: Ling alone said, "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Ling alone said, "No."

sentences.zh: 」於是爭論累日不能決。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche's family lies on the Huai's left; he knows their customs thoroughly, and in generalship and talent there is today none who surpasses him."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche is from the Huai region, knows their ways, and in talent and generalship none today surpasses him."

sentences.zh: 都官尚書裴忌曰：「臣同徐僕射。

translations.literal: Thereupon debate piled up for days without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Debate then lasted days without decision.

sentences.zh: 」陵應聲曰：「非但明徹良將，裴忌即良副也。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Pei Ji said, "Your subject agrees with Vice Director Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of justice Pei Ji said, "I agree with Vice Director Xu."

sentences.zh: 」是日，詔明徹為大都督，令忌監軍事，遂克淮南數十州之地。

translations.literal: Ling answered on the spot, "Not only is Mingche a fine general—Pei Ji is himself a fine deputy."
translations.idiomatic: Ling answered at once, "Mingche is a fine general—and Pei Ji is a fine deputy."

sentences.zh: 高宗因置酒，舉杯屬陵曰：「賞卿知人。

translations.literal: That day an edict made Mingche Grand Commander-in-Chief and ordered Ji to oversee military affairs; they then took several tens of Huainan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: That day Mingche was made grand commander and Ji ordered to oversee the army; they then took dozens of Huainan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 」陵避席對曰：「定策出自聖衷，非臣之力也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan then set out wine, raised his cup, and charged Ling, saying, "I reward you for knowing men."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then raised his cup to Ling: "I reward you for knowing men."

sentences.zh: 」其年加侍中，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Ling left his mat and replied, "The decision came from Your Majesty's sacred mind—it is not this subject's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Ling left his mat and said, "The decision was Your Majesty's—not my strength."

sentences.zh: 七年，領國子祭酒、南徐州大中正。

translations.literal: That year he was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was also made attendant-in-ordinary; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以公事免侍中、僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he concurrently held Director of the National University and Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he also held director of the national university and grand arbiter of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中，給扶，又除領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Because of public business he was removed from attendant-in-ordinary and vice director.
translations.idiomatic: On public business he was removed from attendant-in-ordinary and vice director.

sentences.zh: 八年，加翊右將軍、太子詹事，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made attendant-in-ordinary, granted a staff for support, and again made Commander of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again attendant-in-ordinary, given a support staff, and again commander of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右光祿大夫，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was additionally made Right Supporting General and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with assistant clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was also right supporting general and grand tutor of the heir apparent, with assistant clerks.

sentences.zh: 十年，重為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to right grand master for splendid happiness; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋遷安右將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again became Commander of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he again became commander of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為中書監，領太子詹事，給鼓吹一部，侍中、將軍、右光祿、中正如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was moved to Pacifying Right General and Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made pacifying right general and magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 陵以年老累表求致仕，高宗亦優之，乃詔將作為造大齋，令陵就第攝事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was made Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted one set of martial music, while attendant-in-ordinary, general, right grand master, and grand arbiter remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was director of the secretariat, concurrently grand tutor of the heir apparent, granted martial music; attendant, general, right grand master, and grand arbiter unchanged.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，遷左光祿大夫、太子少傅，餘如故。

translations.literal: Ling, because of age, repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; Emperor Xuan also treated him generously and then ordered the director of palace construction to build a great fast and had Ling conduct affairs at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Ling, being old, repeatedly asked to retire; Emperor Xuan favored him and ordered the director of palace construction to build a great fast hall so Ling could conduct business at home.

sentences.zh: 至德元年卒，時年七十七。

translations.literal: When Houzhu ascended, Ling was moved to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu ascended, Ling was moved to left grand master for splendid happiness and junior tutor of the heir apparent; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「慎終有典，抑乃舊章，令德可甄，諒宜追遠。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Rites for the end have their canon; these restrain the old statutes. Merit that may be weighed should rightly be honored from afar.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Rites for the dead have their canon and restrain the old statutes. Merit that can be weighed should rightly be honored from afar.

sentences.zh: 侍中、安右將軍、左光祿大夫、太子少傅、南徐州大中正建昌縣開國侯陵，弱齡學尚，登朝秀穎，業高名輩，文曰詞宗。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Secure-the-Right General, Left Grand Master of the Glory, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Senior Rectifier of South Xuzhou, and Established Marquis of Jianchang county Ling—from youth his learning was lofty; on entering court he was outstanding; his accomplishment surpassed his generation and his writing made him patriarch of literature.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant, secure-the-right general, left grand master of the glory, junior tutor of the heir apparent, senior rectifier of South Xuzhou, and established marquis of Jianchang county Ling—from youth his learning was lofty; in court he stood out; his achievement surpassed his peers and his writing made him patriarch of letters.

sentences.zh: 朕近歲承華，特相引狎，雖多臥疾，方期克壯，奄然殞逝，震悼于懷。

translations.literal: We in recent years received him at the flowery court and drew him especially close. Though he often lay ill, We still looked for recovery; suddenly he fell and passed away, and shock and grief fill Our breast.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years We received him at court and drew him especially close. Though he often lay ill, We still expected recovery; suddenly he died, and shock and grief fill Our breast.

sentences.zh: 可贈鎮右將軍、特進，其侍中、左光祿、鼓吹、侯如故，并出舉哀，喪事所須，量加資給。

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously granted Secure-the-Right General and Special Advancement; his palace attendant, left grand master of the glory, musical guard, and marquisate remain as before; mourning is to be proclaimed throughout, and funeral needs generously supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted secure-the-right general and special advancement; his palace attendant, left grand master of the glory, musical guard, and marquisate remain as before; mourning is to be proclaimed throughout, and funeral needs generously supplied.

sentences.zh: 諡曰章。」

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Zhang."

sentences.zh: 陵器局深遠，容止可觀，性又清簡，無所營樹，祿俸與親族共之。

translations.literal: Ling's capacity and deportment were deep and far-reaching; his bearing was admirable. His nature was pure and spare; he made no schemes for gain and shared his salary with kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's capacity and bearing were deep and admirable. His nature was pure and spare; he schemed for nothing and shared his salary with kin.

sentences.zh: 太建中，食建昌邑，邑戶送米至于水次，陵親戚有貧匱者，皆令取之，數日便盡，陵家尋致乏絕。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era, while drawing income from Jianchang fief, district households brought grain to the riverside. Poor among his kin he had take it all; in a few days it was gone and his own household soon faced want.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era, while drawing income from Jianchang fief, district households brought grain to the riverside. He had poor kin take it all; in a few days it was gone and his own household soon faced want.

sentences.zh: 府僚怪而問其故。

translations.literal: His office colleagues wondered and asked why.
translations.idiomatic: His office colleagues wondered and asked why.

sentences.zh: 陵云：「我有車牛衣裳可賣，餘家有可賣不？

translations.literal: Ling said: "I have oxen, carts, and clothes to sell—do the rest of you lack things to sell?
translations.idiomatic: Ling said, "I have oxen, carts, and clothes to sell—do the rest of you lack things to sell?

sentences.zh: 」其周給如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his way of aiding others.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his way of aiding others.

sentences.zh: 少而崇信釋教，經論多所精解。

translations.literal: From youth he revered Buddhism and understood many sutras and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he revered Buddhism and understood many sutras and treatises.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，令陵講大品經，義學名僧，自遠雲集，每講筵商較，四座莫能與抗。

translations.literal: When Houzhu was heir apparent he had Ling expound the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra. Eminent monks of doctrine gathered from far off; whenever the lecture hall debated, none in the four seats could match him.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu was heir apparent he had Ling expound the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra. Eminent monks gathered from afar; whenever the lecture hall debated, none in the four seats could match him.

sentences.zh: 目有青睛，時人以為聰惠之相也。

translations.literal: His eyes had blue pupils; contemporaries took this as a mark of keen intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes had blue pupils; contemporaries took this as a mark of keen intelligence.

sentences.zh: 自有陳創業，文檄軍書及禪授詔策，皆陵所製，而九錫尤美。

translations.literal: From Chen's founding, proclamations, military letters, and abdication investiture documents were all Ling's work, and his Nine Bestowals text was especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: From Chen's founding, proclamations, military letters, and abdication investiture documents were all Ling's work, and his Nine Bestowals text was especially fine.

sentences.zh: 為一代文宗，亦不以此矜物，未嘗詆訶作者。

translations.literal: Patriarch of literature for his age, he never lorded this over others and never reviled fellow authors.
