translations.idiomatic: Patriarch of letters for his age, he never lorded it over others and never reviled fellow authors.

sentences.zh: 其於後進之徒，接引無倦。

translations.literal: Toward rising men he showed tireless guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Toward rising men he showed tireless guidance.

sentences.zh: 世祖、高宗之世，國家有大手筆，皆陵草之。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Xuan, whenever the state had a major literary commission, Ling drafted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Xuan, whenever the state had a major literary commission, Ling drafted it.

sentences.zh: 其文頗變舊體，緝裁巧密，多有新意。

translations.literal: His writing greatly altered the old style: tightly woven and ingenious, often with fresh turns.
translations.idiomatic: His writing greatly altered the old style—tightly woven and ingenious, often with fresh turns.

sentences.zh: 每一文出手，好事者已傳寫成誦，遂被之華夷，家藏其本。

translations.literal: Each piece, once issued, admirers copied and recited it; it spread through China and beyond, and households treasured his texts.
translations.idiomatic: Each piece, once issued, admirers copied and recited it; it spread through China and beyond, and households treasured his texts.

sentences.zh: 後逢喪亂，多散失，存者三十卷。

translations.literal: Later came disorder and ruin; most were lost; thirty scrolls survive.
translations.idiomatic: Later came disorder and ruin; most were lost; thirty scrolls survive.

sentences.zh: 有四子：儉，份，儀，僔。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Jian, Fen, Yi, and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jian, Fen, Yi, and Bin.

sentences.zh: 儉一名眾。

translations.literal: Jian also bore the name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also bore the name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 〔二０〕幼而脩立，勤學有志操，汝南周弘正重其為人，妻以女。

translations.literal: [20] From youth upright, diligent in study with firm resolve; Zhou Hongzheng of Runan prized his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: [20] From youth upright, diligent in study with firm resolve; Zhou Hongzheng of Runan prized his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 梁太清初，起家豫章王府行參軍。

translations.literal: At the opening of Liang's Taiqing era he began service as acting aide in the Prince of Yuzhang's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Liang's Taiqing era he began service as acting aide in the Prince of Yuzhang's household.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，陵使魏未反，儉時年二十一，攜老幼避于江陵，梁元帝聞其名，召為尚書金部郎中。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion Ling was on mission to Wei and had not returned; Jian, then twenty-one, took the old and young to refuge at Jiangling. Emperor Yuan of Liang heard his name and summoned him as director in the ministry of the gold office.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Ling was on mission to Wei and had not returned; Jian, then twenty-one, took the old and young to refuge at Jiangling. Emperor Yuan of Liang heard his name and summoned him as director in the ministry of the gold office.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴賦詩，元帝歎賞曰「徐氏之子，復有文矣」。

translations.literal: Once at a feast he was asked to compose verse; Emperor Yuan exclaimed in praise: "The Xu house again has a writer!"
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast he was asked to compose verse; Emperor Yuan exclaimed in praise, "The Xu house again has a writer!"

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，復還於京師。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 永定初，為太子洗馬，遷鎮東從事中郎。

translations.literal: In Yongding's opening he was made steward of the heir apparent, then moved to eastern garrison staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding's opening he was made steward of the heir apparent, then moved to eastern garrison staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 3 he was promoted to secretariat vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 he was promoted to secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 太建初，廣州刺史歐陽紇舉兵反，高宗令儉持節喻旨。

translations.literal: At Taijian's opening Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He raised troops in rebellion; Emperor Xuan ordered Jian to bear credentials and convey the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: At Taijian's opening Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He raised troops in rebellion; Emperor Xuan ordered Jian to bear credentials and convey the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 紇初見儉，盛列仗衛，言辭不恭，儉曰：「呂嘉之事，誠當已遠，將軍獨不見周迪、陳寶應乎？

translations.literal: When He first received Jian he arrayed guards in full strength and spoke with no courtesy. Jian said: "The affair of Lü Jia is indeed far off—has the general alone not seen Zhou Di and Chen Baoying?
translations.idiomatic: When He first received Jian he arrayed guards in full strength and spoke with no courtesy. Jian said, "The affair of Lü Jia is indeed far off—has the general alone not seen Zhou Di and Chen Baoying?

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，未為晚也。

translations.literal: To turn calamity into fortune is not yet too late."
translations.idiomatic: To turn calamity into fortune is not yet too late."

sentences.zh: 」紇默然不答，懼儉沮其眾，不許入城，置儉於孤園寺，遣人守衛，累旬不得還。

translations.literal: He fell silent and did not reply, fearing Jian would sap his followers' morale; he forbade entry to the city and lodged Jian at Guguan Monastery under guard; for many tens of days Jian could not return.
translations.idiomatic: He fell silent and did not reply, fearing Jian would sap his followers' morale; he forbade entry to the city and lodged Jian at Guguan Monastery under guard; for many tens of days Jian could not return.

sentences.zh: 紇嘗出見儉，儉謂之曰：「將軍業已舉事，儉須還報天子，儉之性命雖在將軍，將軍成敗不在於儉，幸不見留。

translations.literal: He once came out to see Jian. Jian told him: "The general has already raised arms; Jian must return to report to Heaven's Son. Jian's life is in the general's hands, but the general's success or failure does not rest on Jian—pray do not detain me."
translations.idiomatic: He once came out to see Jian. Jian told him, "The general has already raised arms; Jian must return to report to Heaven's Son. Jian's life is in the general's hands, but the general's success or failure does not rest on Jian—pray do not detain me."

sentences.zh: 」紇於是乃遣儉從閒道馳還。

translations.literal: He then sent Jian back by a secret road at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Jian back by a secret road at full speed.

sentences.zh: 高宗乃命章昭達率眾討紇，仍以儉悉其形勢，敕儉監昭達軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan then ordered Zhang Zhaoda to lead forces against He and, since Jian knew the situation, charged Jian to supervise Zhaoda's army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then ordered Zhang Zhaoda to lead forces against He and, since Jian knew the situation, charged Jian to supervise Zhaoda's army.

sentences.zh: 紇平，高宗嘉之，賜奴婢十人，米五百斛，除鎮北鄱陽王諮議參軍，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: When He was pacified Emperor Xuan praised him, granted ten slaves and five hundred hu of grain, and made him staff adviser to the Prince of Poyang, pacify-the-north, with concurrent status as secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When He was pacified Emperor Xuan praised him, granted ten slaves and five hundred hu of grain, and made him staff adviser to the pacify-the-north Prince of Poyang with concurrent secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子博士、大匠卿，餘並如故。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to national university academician and director of the grand craftsmen office while keeping the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to national university academician and director of the grand craftsmen office while keeping the rest as before.

sentences.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎，轉太子中庶子，加通直散騎常侍，兼尚書左丞，以公事免。

translations.literal: Soon he was made yellow-gate vice director, then heir apparent's junior mentor, with added direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent left vice director of the masters of writing; he was dismissed for an official matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made yellow-gate vice director, then heir apparent's junior mentor, with added direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent left vice director of the masters of writing; he was dismissed for an official matter.

sentences.zh: 尋起為中衛始興王限外諮議參軍，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as extraordinary staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing in the central guard with concurrent secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as extraordinary staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing in the central guard with concurrent secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 又為太子中庶子，遷貞威將軍、太子左衛率，舍人如故。

translations.literal: Again heir apparent's junior mentor, then steadfast-prestige general and left commandant of the heir's guard while keeping gentleman status.
translations.idiomatic: Again heir apparent's junior mentor, then steadfast-prestige general and left commandant of the heir's guard while keeping gentleman status.

sentences.zh: 後主立，授和戎將軍、宣惠晉熙王長史，行丹陽郡國事。

translations.literal: When Houzhu took the throne he was given harmonious-submission general, chief clerk to the proclaim-grace Prince of Jinxi, with acting charge of Danyang commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he was given harmonious-submission general, chief clerk to the proclaim-grace Prince of Jinxi, with acting charge of Danyang commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄以父憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office on his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋起為和戎將軍，累遷尋陽內史，為政嚴明，盜賊靜息。

translations.literal: Soon recalled as harmonious-submission general, he rose through posts to interior magistrate of Xunyang; his government was strict and clear and banditry subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Soon recalled as harmonious-submission general, he rose through posts to interior magistrate of Xunyang; his government was strict and clear and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，襲封建昌侯，入為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, he inherited the marquisate of Jianchang and entered office as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, he inherited the marquisate of Jianchang and entered office as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 儉性公平，無所阿附，尚書令江總望重一時，亦為儉所糾劾，後主深委任焉。

translations.literal: Jian was fair by nature and fawned on none; Jiang Zong, director of the masters of writing and weighty in his day, was also impeached by Jian—Houzhu trusted him deeply for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was fair by nature and fawned on none; Jiang Zong, director of the masters of writing and weighty in his day, was also impeached by Jian—Houzhu trusted him deeply for it.

sentences.zh: 又領右軍。

translations.literal: He also commanded the right army.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded the right army.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in Zhenming year 2.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenming year 2.

sentences.zh: 份少有父風，年九歲，為夢賦，陵見之，謂所親曰「吾幼屬文，亦不加此」。

translations.literal: Fen from youth had his father's manner; at nine he wrote a Dream Rhapsody. When Ling saw it he told intimates: "I wrote young, yet did not match this."
translations.idiomatic: Fen from youth had his father's manner; at nine he wrote a Dream Rhapsody. When Ling saw it he told intimates, "I wrote young, yet did not match this."

sentences.zh: 解褐為祕書郎，轉太子舍人。

translations.literal: On leaving the commoner's garb he was made secretary gentleman, then heir apparent's chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the commoner's garb he was made secretary gentleman, then heir apparent's chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 累遷豫章王主簿、太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He rose to registrar to the Prince of Yuzhang and steward of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to registrar to the Prince of Yuzhang and steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 出為海鹽令，甚有治績。

translations.literal: Sent out as magistrate of Haiyan, he achieved notable governance.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as magistrate of Haiyan, he achieved notable governance.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，入為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned as steward of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned as steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 份性孝悌，陵嘗遇疾，甚篤，份燒香泣涕，跪誦孝經，晝夜不息，如此者三日，陵疾豁然而愈，親戚皆謂份孝感所致。

translations.literal: Fen was filial and brotherly. When Ling once fell gravely ill, Fen burned incense, wept, knelt, and recited the Classic of Filial Piety without cease day and night for three days; Ling's illness suddenly lifted, and kin all said Fen's filial feeling had moved Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fen was filial and brotherly. When Ling once fell gravely ill, Fen burned incense, wept, knelt, and recited the Classic of Filial Piety without cease day and night for three days; Ling's illness suddenly lifted, and kin all said Fen's filial feeling had moved Heaven.

sentences.zh: 太建二年卒，時年二十二。

translations.literal: He died in Taijian year 2, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taijian year 2, aged twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 儀少聰警，以周易生舉高第為祕書郎，出為烏傷令。

translations.literal: Yi was keen and alert from youth; as a student of the Changes he ranked high and became secretary gentleman, then went out as magistrate of Wushang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was keen and alert from youth; as a student of the Changes he ranked high and became secretary gentleman, then went out as magistrate of Wushang.

sentences.zh: 禎明初，遷尚書殿中郎，尋兼東宮學士。

translations.literal: At Zhenming's opening he was promoted to palace gentleman of the masters of writing, soon with concurrent eastern-palace academician.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenming's opening he was promoted to palace gentleman of the masters of writing, soon with concurrent eastern-palace academician.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，隱于錢塘之赭山，煬帝召為學士，尋除著作郎。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang year 9 he retired to Zhe Mountain in Qiantang; Emperor Yang summoned him as academician and soon made him director in the works office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 9 he retired to Zhe Mountain in Qiantang; Emperor Yang summoned him as academician and soon made him director in the works office.

sentences.zh: 大業四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in Daye year 4.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daye year 4.

sentences.zh: 孝克，陵之第三弟也。

translations.literal: Xiaoke was Ling's third younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke was Ling's third younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少為周易生，有口辯，能談玄理。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student of the Changes, eloquent, and able to discourse on Neo-Daoist principle.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a student of the Changes, eloquent, and able to discourse on Neo-Daoist principle.

sentences.zh: 既長，遍通五經，博覽史籍，亦善屬文，而文不逮義。

translations.literal: Grown, he mastered the Five Classics, read widely in histories, and wrote well, yet his writing did not match his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered the Five Classics, read widely in histories, and wrote well, yet his writing did not match his learning.

sentences.zh: 梁太清初，起家為太學博士。

translations.literal: At Liang Taiqing's opening he began as academician of the imperial university.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang Taiqing's opening he began as academician of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，遭父憂，殆不勝喪，事所生母陳氏，盡就養之道。

translations.literal: Utterly filial, on his father's mourning he nearly could not bear the grief; toward his birth mother Lady Chen he fulfilled every duty of support.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial, on his father's mourning he nearly could not bear the grief; toward his birth mother Lady Chen he fulfilled every duty of support.

sentences.zh: 梁末，侯景寇亂，京邑大飢，餓死者十八九。

translations.literal: At Liang's end Hou Jing ravaged the realm; the capital knew great famine and eight or nine in ten starved.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang's end Hou Jing ravaged the realm; the capital knew great famine and eight or nine in ten starved.

sentences.zh: 孝克養母，饘粥不能給，妻東莞臧氏，領軍將軍臧盾之女也，甚有容色，孝克乃謂之曰：「今飢荒如此，供養交闕，欲嫁卿與富人，望彼此俱濟，於卿意如何？

translations.literal: Xiaoke supported his mother but gruel could not suffice. His wife was Lady Zang of Dongguan, daughter of the garrison general Zang Dun, very fair of face. Xiaoke told her: "Famine is such that support fails on every side. I wish to marry you to a rich man in hope that we may all be saved—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke supported his mother but gruel could not suffice. His wife was Lady Zang of Dongguan, daughter of the garrison general Zang Dun, very fair of face. Xiaoke told her, "Famine is such that support fails on every side. I wish to marry you to a rich man in hope that we may all be saved—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」臧氏弗之許也。

translations.literal: " Lady Zang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Zang would not agree.

sentences.zh: 時有孔景行者，為侯景將，富於財，孝克密因媒者陳意，景行多從左右，逼而迎之，臧涕泣而去，所得穀帛，悉以供養。

translations.literal: There was Kong Jingxing, a general under Hou Jing, rich in wealth. Xiaoke secretly had a go-between present his wish; Jingxing came with many attendants and forced the marriage. Lady Zang left in tears; all grain and silk gained went wholly to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: There was Kong Jingxing, a general under Hou Jing, rich in wealth. Xiaoke secretly had a go-between present his wish; Jingxing came with many attendants and forced the marriage. Lady Zang left in tears; all grain and silk gained went wholly to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 孝克又剃髮為沙門，改名法整，兼乞食以充給焉。

translations.literal: Xiaoke also shaved his head as a monk, took the name Fazheng, and begged food to fill the need.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke also shaved his head as a monk, took the name Fazheng, and begged food to fill the need.

sentences.zh: 臧氏亦深念舊恩，數私致饋餉，故不乏絕。

translations.literal: Lady Zang too cherished the old bond and often sent gifts in secret, so want never cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zang too cherished the old bond and often sent gifts in secret, so want never cut them off.

sentences.zh: 後景行戰死，臧伺孝克於途中，累日乃見，謂孝克曰：「往日之事，非為相負，今既得脫，當歸供養。

translations.literal: Later Jingxing died in battle. Lady Zang watched for Xiaoke on the road; many days passed before she saw him. She said: "What passed before was no betrayal on my part. Now I am free—I should return to support your household."
translations.idiomatic: Later Jingxing died in battle. Lady Zang watched for Xiaoke on the road; many days passed before she saw him. She said, "What passed before was no betrayal on my part. Now I am free—I should return to support your household."

sentences.zh: 」孝克默然無答。

translations.literal: Xiaoke was silent and gave no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke was silent and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 於是歸俗，更為夫妻。

translations.literal: He then returned to lay life and they became husband and wife again.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to lay life and they became husband and wife again.

sentences.zh: 後東遊，居于錢塘之佳義里，與諸僧討論釋典，遂通三論。

translations.literal: Later he traveled east and lived in Jiayi lane in Qiantang, debating Buddhist sutras with monks until he mastered the Three Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled east and lived in Jiayi lane in Qiantang, debating Buddhist sutras with monks until he mastered the Three Treatises.

sentences.zh: 每日二時講，旦講佛經，晚講禮傳，道俗受業者數百人。

translations.literal: Each day he lectured twice: mornings on Buddhist sutras, evenings on the Rites and Classics; clergy and laity studying under him numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he lectured twice: mornings on Buddhist sutras, evenings on the Rites and Classics; clergy and laity studying under him numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，除剡令，非其好也，尋復去職。

translations.literal: In Tianjia he was made magistrate of Shan—not to his liking; soon he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia he was made magistrate of Shan—not to his liking; soon he resigned.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，徵為祕書丞，不就，乃蔬食長齋，持菩薩戒，晝夜講誦法華經，高宗甚嘉其操行。

translations.literal: In Taijian year 4 he was summoned as secretariat aide but did not accept; he took vegetable food and long fasting, kept the bodhisattva precepts, and day and night chanted the Lotus Sutra—Emperor Xuan greatly praised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 he was summoned as secretariat aide but did not accept; he took vegetable food and long fasting, kept the bodhisattva precepts, and day and night chanted the Lotus Sutra—Emperor Xuan greatly praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 六年，除國子博士，遷通直散騎常侍，兼國子祭酒，尋為真。

translations.literal: In year 6 he was made national university academician, promoted to direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with concurrent rector of the national university, soon confirmed in the latter post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made national university academician, promoted to direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with concurrent rector of the national university, soon confirmed in the latter post.

sentences.zh: 孝克每侍宴，無所食噉，至席散，當其前膳羞損減，高宗密記以問中書舍人管斌，斌不能對。

translations.literal: Whenever Xiaoke attended banquets he ate nothing; when the feast ended the delicacies before him were diminished. Emperor Xuan secretly noted this and asked secretariat gentleman Guan Bin, who could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiaoke attended banquets he ate nothing; when the feast ended the delicacies before him were diminished. Emperor Xuan secretly noted this and asked secretariat gentleman Guan Bin, who could not answer.

sentences.zh: 自是斌以意伺之，見孝克取珍果內紳帶中，斌當時莫識其意，後更尋訪，方知還以遺母。

translations.literal: From then Bin watched him by intent and saw Xiaoke tuck fine fruit into his sash. At the time Bin did not grasp his meaning; later inquiry showed he brought them home for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: From then Bin watched him by intent and saw Xiaoke tuck fine fruit into his sash. At the time Bin did not grasp his meaning; later inquiry showed he brought them home for his mother.

sentences.zh: 斌以實啟，高宗嗟歎良久，乃敕所司，自今宴享，孝克前饌，並遣將還，以餉其母，時論美之。

translations.literal: Bin reported the fact; Emperor Xuan sighed long in praise and ordered that from then on at feasts Xiaoke's serving before him be all sent back to nourish his mother—contemporaries praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Bin reported the fact; Emperor Xuan sighed long in praise and ordered that from then on at feasts Xiaoke's serving before him be all sent back to nourish his mother—contemporaries praised this.

sentences.zh: 至德中，皇太子入學釋奠，百司陪列，孝克發孝經題，後主詔皇太子北面致敬。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era the heir apparent entered school for the libation-offering sacrifice; all offices stood in attendance. Xiaoke opened the Classic of Filial Piety as topic; Houzhu ordered the heir to face north and bow in respect.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era the heir apparent entered school for the libation-offering sacrifice; all offices stood in attendance. Xiaoke opened the Classic of Filial Piety as topic; Houzhu ordered the heir to face north and bow in respect.

sentences.zh: 孝克性清素而好施惠，故不免飢寒，後主敕以石頭津稅給之，孝克悉用設齋寫經，隨得隨盡。

translations.literal: Xiaoke was plain and fond of giving, so he could not escape hunger and cold. Houzhu ordered the Shitou ferry toll granted him; Xiaoke used it all for feasts and copying sutras, spending each sum as it came.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke was plain and fond of giving, so he could not escape hunger and cold. Houzhu ordered the Shitou ferry toll granted him; Xiaoke used it all for feasts and copying sutras, spending each sum as it came.

sentences.zh: 二年，為散騎常侍，侍東宮。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and attended the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and attended the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隨例入關。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered the passes by the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered the passes by the usual rule.

sentences.zh: 家道壁立，所生母患，欲粳米為粥，不能常辦。

translations.literal: His household stood bare; his birth mother fell ill and wanted polished rice for porridge—he could not always provide it.
translations.idiomatic: His household stood bare; his birth mother fell ill and wanted polished rice for porridge—he could not always provide it.

sentences.zh: 母亡之後，孝克遂常噉麥，有遺粳米者，孝克對而悲泣，終身不復食之焉。

translations.literal: After his mother died Xiaoke ate barley regularly; when polished rice was sent as a gift he wept before it and never ate it again in his life.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died Xiaoke ate barley regularly; when polished rice was sent as a gift he wept before it and never ate it again in his life.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年，長安疾疫，隋文帝聞其名行，召令於尚書都堂講金剛般若經。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang year 10 Chang'an suffered plague; Emperor Wen of Sui heard his fame and conduct and summoned him to expound the Diamond Prajna Sutra in the main hall of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 10 Chang'an suffered plague; Emperor Wen of Sui heard his fame and conduct and summoned him to expound the Diamond Prajna Sutra in the main hall of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 尋授國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made national university academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made national university academician.

sentences.zh: 後侍東宮講禮傳。

translations.literal: Later he attended the eastern palace lecturing on the Rites and Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attended the eastern palace lecturing on the Rites and Classics.

sentences.zh: 十九年以疾卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In year 19 he died of illness, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he died of illness, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 臨終，正坐念佛，室內有非常異香氣，鄰里皆驚異之。

translations.literal: At the end he sat upright chanting the Buddha's name; a rare strange fragrance filled the room and neighbors were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he sat upright chanting the Buddha's name; a rare strange fragrance filled the room and neighbors were all astonished.

sentences.zh: 子萬載，仕至晉安王功曹史、太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His son Wanzai served up to clerk on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an and steward of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wanzai served up to clerk on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an and steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：徐孝穆挺五行之秀，稟天地之靈，聰明特達，籠罩今古。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xu Xiaomu drew the finest of the five phases and received Heaven and Earth's spirit—keen intelligence that embraced past and present.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xu Xiaomu drew the finest of the five phases and received Heaven and Earth's spirit—keen intelligence that embraced past and present.

sentences.zh: 及締構興王，遭逢泰運，位隆朝宰，獻替謀猷，蓋亮直存矣。

translations.literal: When he helped frame the rising dynasty and met a great fortune, he rose to foremost minister and offered counsel in and out—plainly the upright heart remained.
translations.idiomatic: When he helped frame the rising dynasty and met a great fortune, he rose to foremost minister and offered counsel in and out—plainly the upright heart remained.

sentences.zh: 孝克砥身厲行，養親逾禮，亦參、閔之志歟。

translations.literal: Xiaoke honed body and conduct and nurtured kin beyond the rites—is this not the resolve of Zeng Shen and Min Ziqian?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke honed body and conduct and nurtured kin beyond the rites—is this not the resolve of Zeng Shen and Min Ziqian?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 梁普通二年晉安王為平西將軍寧蠻校尉 按梁書簡文帝紀，晉安王蕭綱為平西將軍寧蠻校尉在梁武帝普通四年。

translations.literal: [1] "In Liang Putong year 2 the Prince of Jin'an was made pacifying-west general and colonel pacifying the barbarians"—according to the Annals of Emperor Jianwen in the Book of Liang, the Prince of Jin'an Xiao Gang received those posts in Liang Wudi's Putong year 4.
translations.idiomatic: On "In Liang Putong year 2 the Prince of Jin'an was made pacifying-west general and colonel pacifying the barbarians": according to the Annals of Emperor Jianwen in the Book of Liang, the Prince of Jin'an Xiao Gang received those posts in Liang Wudi's Putong year 4.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 〔中〕大通

translations.literal: [2] [zhong] Datong
translations.idiomatic: [2] [zhong] Datong

translations.literal: (two)
translations.idiomatic: (two)

sentences.zh: 〔三〕年王立為皇太子 據梁書武帝紀補改。

translations.literal: [Three] years, the prince was established as crown prince—supplemented and emended according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On "[three] years, the prince was established as crown prince": emended per the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of Liang.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕 則有日

translations.literal: [Three] Then there was a sun
translations.idiomatic: [Three] Then there was a sun

translations.literal: (bird)
translations.idiomatic: (bird)

sentences.zh: 〔烏〕流災 據徐孝穆集及嚴可均輯全陳文改。

translations.literal: [Crow] streams calamity—changed according to Xu Xiaomu's Collected Works and Yan Kejun's Collected Chen Documents.
translations.idiomatic: On "[crow] streams calamity": emended per Xu Xiaomu's Collected Works and Yan Kejun's Collected Chen Documents.

sentences.zh: 按相傳日中有烏，見淮南子精神訓。

translations.literal: Comment: tradition says there is a crow in the sun, as in the Spiritual Teachings chapter of the Huainanzi.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says there is a crow in the sun, as in Huainanzi, Spiritual Teachings.

sentences.zh: 又傳堯時十日並出，草木焦枯，堯命羿仰射十日，中其九，烏皆死，墮羽翼，見北堂書鈔一四九、藝文類聚一、御覽三引淮南子。

translations.literal: Also tradition says that in Yao's time ten suns appeared together and plants withered; Yao ordered Yi to shoot upward at the ten suns, hit nine, and the crows all died and fell with their wings—as cited in Northern Hall Manuscripts 149, Literary Gatherings 1, and Imperial Readings 3 quoting the Huainanzi.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition also says ten suns rose in Yao's time, plants withered, and Yao had Yi shoot nine of them so the crows fell—cited in Northern Hall Manuscripts 149, Literary Gatherings 1, and Imperial Readings 3 from Huainanzi.

sentences.zh: 為此語所本。

translations.literal: This is the source of the phrase.
translations.idiomatic: That is the source of the phrase.

sentences.zh: 〔四〕 方今越常藐藐 「越常」各本作「越裳」。

translations.literal: [4] Now Yuechang stands remote—"Yuechang" in all editions reads "Yueshang."
translations.idiomatic: On "now Yuechang stands remote": all editions read Yueshang for Yuechang.

sentences.zh: 按常裳古今字。

translations.literal: Comment: chang and shang are ancient and modern forms of the same word.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and shang are ancient and modern forms of the same word.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕 泉流寶碗 「碗」吳兆宜徐孝穆集箋注本作「盎」，注引藝林伐山，云寶盎泉出江州。

translations.literal: [5] Springs flow, treasure bowls—"bowl" in Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads "vessel," with a note citing Forest of Literary Arts citing Woodcutter on Mountains, saying the Treasure Vessel Spring issues from Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On "springs flow, treasure bowls": Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads vessel for bowl, citing Forest of Literary Arts and Woodcutter on Mountains on the Treasure Vessel Spring at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 〔六〕 又此賓遊 「此」字下元龜六六三及徐孝穆集箋注本並有「 段」字。

translations.literal: [6] Again, these guest-travelers—below "this" both Yuan Gui 663 and the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection have the character "segment."
translations.idiomatic: On "again, these guest-travelers": Yuan Gui 663 and the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection add segment below this.

sentences.zh: 〔七〕 四冢磔蚩尤 「四」當作「三」。

translations.literal: [7] Four tombs dismembering Chiyou—"four" should read "three."
translations.idiomatic: On "four tombs dismembering Chiyou": four should read three.

sentences.zh: 相傳堯磔蚩尤，身首異處，分葬三處，其首冢在壽陽，其肩膂冢在山陽，其髀冢在鉅鹿，見雲笈七籤引軒轅本紀，為此語所本。

translations.literal: Tradition says Yao dismembered Chiyou, body and head in different places, buried in three sites—the head tomb at Shouyang, the shoulder tomb at Shanyang, the thigh tomb at Julu—as in Cloud Book Seven Talismans citing Records of the Yellow Emperor; this is the source of the phrase.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says Yao dismembered Chiyou and buried head, shoulders, and thighs at Shouyang, Shanyang, and Julu—Cloud Book Seven Talismans citing Records of the Yellow Emperor is the source.

sentences.zh: 梁書元帝紀載徐陵勸進表，亦有「 蚩尤三冢，寧謂嚴誅」之語。

translations.literal: The Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan in the History of Liang records Xu Ling's petition urging accession, which also has "Chiyou's three tombs—can one call it stern execution?"
translations.idiomatic: Liang Emperor Yuan's annals record Xu Ling's accession petition with the same "Chiyou's three tombs—can one call it stern execution?"

sentences.zh: 〔八〕 又聞本朝公主 「公主」徐孝穆集及嚴輯全陳文並作「王公」，疑作「王公」是。

translations.literal: [8] Again heard that this dynasty's princesses—"princesses" in Xu Xiaomu's Collected Works and Yan's Collected Chen Documents both read "princes and dukes"; probably "princes and dukes" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: On "again heard that this dynasty's princesses": Xu Xiaomu's Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read princes and dukes; that is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 〔九〕 舂舂井井 嚴輯全陳文作「鄉井鄉邑」。

translations.literal: [9] Chunchun jingjing—Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads "native hamlet, native district."
translations.idiomatic: On "chunchun jingjing": Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads native hamlet, native district.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕虞哥引路 「哥」各本作「歌」。

translations.literal: [10] Yu Ge showed the way—"ge" in all editions reads "song."
translations.idiomatic: On "Yu Ge showed the way": all editions read song for ge.

sentences.zh: 按哥即古歌字。

translations.literal: Comment: ge is the ancient form of the character for song.
translations.idiomatic: Ge is the ancient form of the character for song.

sentences.zh: 〔一一〕吾知其決 「決」當作「訣」。

translations.literal: [11] I know its secret—"secret" should read "formula."
translations.idiomatic: On "I know its secret": secret (jue) should read formula (jue).

sentences.zh: 今本徐孝穆集及嚴輯全陳文並作「訣」。

translations.literal: The current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents both read "formula."
translations.idiomatic: Current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents both read formula.

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕其外膏脣販舌 「販舌」徐孝穆集箋注本改「拭舌」，注引後漢書宦者呂強傳「群邪項領，膏脣拭舌」。

translations.literal: [12] Besides, greasy lips and vending tongues—"vending tongue" in Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection is changed to "wiping tongue," the note citing the Biography of the eunuch Lü Qiang in Later Han: "the wicked crane their necks, greasy lips wipe tongue."
translations.idiomatic: On "greasy lips and vending tongues": Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads wiping tongue, citing Later Han, Biography of Lü Qiang: "the wicked crane their necks, greasy lips wipe tongue."

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕莫不崇君親以銘物 「銘」今本徐孝穆集及嚴輯全陳文並作「詔」。

translations.literal: [13] None fail to honor lord and kin to inscribe things—"inscribe" in the current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads "charge."
translations.idiomatic: On "none fail to honor lord and kin to inscribe things": current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read charge for inscribe.

sentences.zh: 〔一四〕巡省方化 今本徐孝穆集及嚴輯全陳文並作「巡方省化」，按巡方省化與下東序西膠相對成文，作「巡方省化」是。

translations.literal: [14] Touring provinces to transform customs—the current Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read "touring the regions to inspect transformation"; as touring the regions pairs with the eastern and western sequences below, "touring the regions" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: On "touring provinces to transform customs": current texts read touring the regions to inspect transformation, which pairs with eastern and western sequences below and is correct.

sentences.zh: 〔一五〕東序西膠 按徐孝穆集箋注本改為「西序東膠」，注引禮王制「夏后氏養庶老於西序，周人養國老於東膠」。

translations.literal: [15] Eastern sequence, western college—the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection changes to "western sequence, eastern college," citing Royal Regulations: "The Xia housed common elders in the western sequence; Zhou housed state elders in the eastern college."
translations.idiomatic: On "eastern sequence, western college": the annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection reads western sequence, eastern college, citing Royal Regulations on Xia and Zhou elder care.

sentences.zh: 〔一六〕非豹非貔 「豹」徐孝穆集箋注本及嚴輯全陳文並作「虎」。

translations.literal: [16] Not leopard, not bear—"leopard" in Wu Zhaoyi's annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents reads "tiger."
translations.idiomatic: On "not leopard, not bear": annotated Xu Xiaomu Collection and Yan's Collected Chen Documents read tiger for leopard.

sentences.zh: 按語本書牧誓「尚桓桓，如虎如貔」。

translations.literal: Comment: the phrase comes from Announcement of Mu: "Be bold and martial, like tigers, like bears."
translations.idiomatic: The phrase comes from Announcement of Mu: "Be bold and martial, like tigers, like bears."

sentences.zh: 梁書元帝紀載陵勸進表亦有「非虎非貔」語。

translations.literal: The History of Liang, Emperor Yuan's annals, records Ling's petition urging accession also has "not tiger, not bear."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Emperor Yuan's annals record Xu Ling's accession petition with the same "not tiger, not bear."

sentences.zh: 此作「豹」，乃避唐諱改。

translations.literal: This reads "leopard" because of alteration to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Leopard here is a Tang-taboo alteration.

sentences.zh: 〔一七〕時安成王頊為司空 「頊」原作「諱」，思廉原文如此，今據北監本、汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [17] At that time Prince of Ancheng Xu was minister of works—"Xu" was originally written "taboo name"; Sizhi's original text is so; now changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "at that time Prince of Ancheng Xu was minister of works": Xu was written taboo name in Yao Sizhi's original; emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 〔一八〕直兵鮑僧叡假王威權 「鮑僧叡」北監本、汲本、殿本作「 鮑叔叡」。

translations.literal: [18] Duty officer Bao Shenrui abused the prince's authority—"Bao Shenrui" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "Bao Shurui."
translations.idiomatic: On "duty officer Bao Shenrui abused the prince's authority": Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read Bao Shurui.

sentences.zh: 〔一九〕三年遷尚書左僕射 「三年」各本並訛「二年」。

translations.literal: [19] In the third year he was promoted to left vice minister of the Secretariat—"third year" in all editions is erroneously "second year."
translations.idiomatic: On "in the third year he was promoted to left vice minister of the Secretariat": all editions wrongly read second year.

sentences.zh: 按宣帝紀，三年春正月癸丑，以尚書右僕射領大著作徐陵為尚書僕射，四年春正月丙午，以尚書僕射領大著作徐陵為尚書左僕射，與此異。

translations.literal: Comment: in Emperor Xuan's annals, third year, first month, guichou, Xu Ling as right vice minister of the Secretariat and director of the great works was made vice minister of the Secretariat; fourth year, first month, bingwu, as vice minister of the Secretariat and director of the great works he was made left vice minister—this differs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan's annals place Xu Ling's promotion to vice minister in year 3, guichou, and to left vice minister in year 4, bingwu—not as here.

sentences.zh: 〔二０〕儉一名眾 殿本考證云：「『眾』南史作『報』。」

translations.literal: [20] Jian's other name was Zhong—the Hall edition's textual verification says: "'Zhong' in the Southern History reads 'Bao.'"
translations.idiomatic: On "Jian's other name was Zhong": the Hall edition notes the Southern History reads Bao for Zhong.
